areas.name: CLI, config, input files, baseline and drift
areas.coverage: Read in full at bc7090d (detached worktree .claude/review-r4/scratch/find-A01, npm ci --ignore-scripts and npm run build OK; worktree removed at the end): src/cli.ts, src/config.ts, src/input-file.ts, src/baseline.ts, src/report/drift.ts. Read in part: src/redact.ts (tiers, TRIVIAL), src/protocol/trace.ts createRedactor, src/diagnose.ts schemeSuggestion, src/protocol/legacy.ts paginate, src/snapshot.ts emptySnapshot, src/report/index.ts buildReport failed/gate. Also the README stability policy, docs/guide/ci.md baseline recipes, round 3 FINDINGS.md (A01 rows and improvements) and REMEDIATION.md, the CHANGELOG 1.1.0 and 1.0.1 CLI items, and grepped round 1 for drift. Ran against the built CLI: good-server baseline save and reuse; fatal-run overwrite through --output json and --json-output (A01-02); drift with a tampered fingerprint in text, json, junit and sarif with GITHUB_ACTIONS (A01-01); a listing-only run with --fail-on-drift (A01-04); a local 401 server on 127.0.0.1 with --fail-on-incomplete --save-baseline (A01-03); config files with NUL in stdio args, env, header and cwd (A01-06); 11 parseArgs error cases (none echoes a value); 9 URL/scheme usage-error cases (heuristics behave as documented; not reported). Unit-level timing of knownFindings through dist/baseline.js (A01-05). Not done: vitest files (not needed for the repros), the Windows/macOS case-folding paths of samePath, the signal-exit path, the phase line on a real TTY, the modern-server.ts fixture, and redacted-name drift pairing beyond reading the code. One positional test ('https://h/x#tokenvalue') unintentionally started a check against the dotless host 'h' (DNS lookup only, no server reached). No fixed round-3 item was found to have regressed.

improvements.title: Bootstrap a baseline from config without exit 2
improvements.detail: A config file with baseline and failOnDrift or diffOnly cannot do the first run: 'cannot read --baseline: no such file' is exit 2, so users must keep two configs or pass --no-fail-on-drift and drop the key. Add --baseline-optional (config key baselineOptional): a missing baseline file means no baseline, with a stderr note, and --fail-on-drift/--diff-only are then inactive with a note.

improvements.title: Say on stderr when the command line's server replaces the config file's server
improvements.detail: When an explicit --config has url or stdio and the command line also names a server, the file's server is ignored silently. The 'options from --config X' line says nothing, while env/cwd/header drops get a 'not used from' note. Add 'key "url" (a server is given on the command line)' to that note.

improvements.title: Protect input files from being overwritten by outputs
improvements.detail: samePath guards --output against --save-baseline, --json-output and --baseline only. --output, --json-output or --save-baseline can still overwrite the --config file, --tool-args, --openai-manifest or $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. Extend the same check to every input path.

improvements.title: Stable SARIF fingerprint per drift change content
improvements.detail: BASE-001 partialFingerprints hash only kind and tool name, so a later, different change to the same tool (description, then inputSchema) has the same fingerprint as an earlier dismissed or fixed alert. Include the sorted changed fields, or the new sha256, in the fingerprint so that code scanning treats a new change as a new alert. Source: SARIF 2.1.0 §3.27.17 partialFingerprints, https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/sarif-v2.1.0.html

improvements.title: UTF-16BE config/baseline/tool-args decoding
improvements.detail: readToolArgs, loadConfig and readBaseline decode UTF-16LE with a BOM but not UTF-16BE (FE FF), which then fails as 'not valid JSON'. Decode it too, or name the encoding in the error.

improvements.title: Lean baseline document
improvements.detail: --save-baseline writes the full JSON report (snapshot included). --baseline needs only findings (ruleId, platforms, tool, resource, path, message) and toolFingerprints. A --save-baseline that writes a lean document, still valid for --baseline, keeps baselines far under the 16 MiB INPUT_FILE_CAP and makes git diffs of committed baselines readable.

findings.title: --fail-on-drift exits 1 while every report format says PASS
findings.claim: Under --fail-on-drift, a tool change (or tools that could not be compared) makes the exit code 1, but buildReport is never told about it. The text Result line reads 'Result: PASS (--fail-on error)', JSON summary.failed is false and gate.reason is null, JUnit has failures="0", and under GITHUB_ACTIONS no ::error annotation explains the exit 1. In the not-compared case the only trace is one stderr line. Round 3 fixed the same mismatch for --fail-on-incomplete (A10-01, medium); --fail-on-drift was left out. The Action and other tools that read summary.failed from the JSON see a passing run that the job failed.
findings.repro: RAN: save a baseline from good-server, then set toolFingerprints[0].sha256 and .fields.description to 64 zeros in a copy bd.json. `node dist/cli.js --baseline bd.json --fail-on-drift --stdio -- node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs` gives exit 1, prints '~ search_notes: changed: description' and 'Result: PASS (--fail-on error)'. The same with `--format json` gives exit 1 and summary {failed:false, gate.reason:null}. With `--format junit`: failures="0". With GITHUB_ACTIONS=true --format sarif: exit 1, and stderr has only the local banner.
findings.fix: Pass the drift outcome into buildReport, as was done for failOnIncomplete: when failOnDrift && (changes>0 || notCompared), set summary.failed=true, gate.reason='tool definitions changed since baseline (--fail-on-drift)' or 'tool definitions not compared (--fail-on-drift)', a Result line 'FAIL (... --fail-on-drift)', a JUnit <failure>/<error> and one GitHub ::error. The exit code stays the same, so this fits a patch.

votes.evidence:
I read the code at bc7090d with git show and did not run anything. src/cli.ts:789 calls buildReport(..., failOnSpec, failOnIncomplete) and never passes a drift flag. Drift is computed after the report exists (798-799) and only reaches the exit code at line 835: `report.summary.failed || textOpts.failOnDrift || notCompared ? 1 : 0`. In src/report/index.ts:56-71, summary.failed = failed || incompleteFails || fatal || stopped, and gate.reason gets only the --fail-on-incomplete text. resultLine (index.ts:188+) reads only report.summary, so a drift-only failure prints 'Result: PASS'. annotations(report) (cli.ts:813) gets no drift, so no ::error is written. junit.ts:107 says drift is listed in system-out and is "never a failure". In action.yml:195-196 the action sets its `verdict` output to PASS when summary.failed is false, while its exit-code output is 1. In the not-compared case changes=0, so neither the heading note nor the summary-line note appears and the only trace is the stderr line at 834. Nothing elsewhere guards against this, so the mismatch is real.

Severity is reduced because this is partly documented on purpose. docs/guide/options-and-config.md:23 says "The verdicts and `summary.failed` stay about findings", and docs/design/spec.md:1317 says only "the section heading and the --output summary line say so". In text and markdown, the drift heading (drift.ts:188) does add "fails the run (--fail-on-drift)" when tools changed, so "every format says PASS" overstates it a little.

The doc wording still conflicts with itself. options-and-config.md:140 says the Result line and summary.gate "name what failed the run", but they read PASS with gate.reason null on exit 1. The Action's verdict output (PASS next to exit-code 1) is a real consumer-facing contradiction. This is the same class of mismatch as A10-01, but since summary.failed is documented this way and the text heading signals the failure when tools changed, I rate it low rather than medium.

I built bc7090d in a detached worktree, which I have since removed. In src/cli.ts:789, buildReport(...) receives failOn, failOnSpec and failOnIncomplete but nothing about drift. textOpts.failOnDrift and notCompared are only used in the exit code at line 835 (`report.summary.failed || textOpts.failOnDrift || notCompared ? 1 : 0`), so summary.failed and gate.reason never include drift. src/report/index.ts:56-71 handles only incompleteFails.

Repro: I saved a baseline from good-server.mjs, then set toolFingerprints[0].sha256 and fields.description to 64 zeros. Results with `--baseline bd.json --fail-on-drift`:
- text: exit 1. It prints '~ search_notes: changed: description' and 'Result: PASS (--fail-on error)'. The only signal is the section heading 'CHANGED TOOL DEFINITIONS (1 since baseline) · fails the run (--fail-on-drift)', which contradicts the PASS line.
- `--format json`: exit 1, summary.failed=false, gate.reason=null. The JSON has no drift field.
- `--format junit`: exit 1, failures="0".
- `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true --format sarif`: exit 1, and stderr has only the 'Local target: ...' banner. There is no ::error annotation.

This is the same kind of report/exit mismatch fixed for --fail-on-incomplete in A10-01 (medium). The flag is opt-in and the text output names the drift once, so medium fits.

findings.title: A failed or stopped run still overwrites the baseline through --output (format json) or --json-output
findings.claim: The A01-02 fix in 1.0.1 skips only --save-baseline when the run is fatal (exit 3) or stopped (exit 4). The comment at cli.ts:630 calls '--output in --format json' over the --baseline file 'the intended refresh', and docs/guide/ci.md:57 says --save-baseline writes 'the same document as --format json --output <file>'. Those paths, and --json-output pointed at the baseline file, are still written on exit 3/4. The result is the round-3 scenario again: the accepted baseline is replaced by a connect-failure report with toolFingerprints null. When --save-baseline and --json-output name the same file, stderr even says 'the earlier baseline, if any, is kept', then 'JSON report written to b3.json', and the file is overwritten.
findings.repro: RAN: (1) `node dist/cli.js --baseline b.json --format json --output b.json --stdio -- node -e 'process.exit(1)'` gives exit 3, and b.json now has 3 findings and toolFingerprints null. A later `--baseline b.json --fail-on-drift` run against good-server exits 1 with 'tool definitions not compared ... re-save the baseline'. (2) `node dist/cli.js --baseline b3.json --save-baseline b3.json --json-output b3.json --stdio -- node -e 'process.exit(1)'` gives exit 3 and the stderr lines 'warning: --save-baseline not written ... the earlier baseline, if any, is kept' and 'JSON report written to b3.json'. b3.json is overwritten (toolFingerprints null).
findings.fix: When unsaved (fatal or stopped), skip every output whose path samePath()s the --baseline file or the --save-baseline file. That covers --output in json format and --json-output; print the same 'not written' warning and keep the exit code. Fix the misleading 'is kept' message for the case where another output names the same file, and update the cli.ts:630 comment and ci.md:57 ('the same document, except that it is not written on exit 3 or 4').

votes.evidence: Reproduced at bc7090d. In cli.ts:847-856, `unsaved` skips only the `--save-baseline` entry (`if (flag === '--save-baseline' && unsaved) continue`). `--json-output` and `--output` are still written on exit 3 or 4. (1) The command `--baseline b.json --format json --output b.json --stdio -- node -e 'process.exit(1)'` exits 3 and b.json then has toolFingerprints null and 3 findings. cli.ts:630 calls this path 'the intended refresh'. (2) With `--save-baseline b3.json --json-output b3.json` on the same failed command, stderr prints 'warning: --save-baseline not written: the run did not connect; the earlier baseline, if any, is kept' and then 'JSON report written to s/b3.json'. The file is overwritten (toolFingerprints null), so the message is wrong. Low severity: the user named that path for the output.

findings.title: --save-baseline is written by a run that exits 3 under --fail-on-incomplete
findings.claim: `unsaved` covers only snap.fatal and limits.stopped. With --fail-on-incomplete, a partial run (auth-required, token rejected, tools/list failed) exits 3, which the help documents as a failed run. It still replaces the baseline with a report that has no tool findings and toolFingerprints null; the only sign is a stderr warning. An expired CI token in the documented default-branch refresh job therefore makes the next MR runs fail: every finding is new and drift is not compared.
findings.repro: RAN: a 127.0.0.1:18765 server that answers every request with 401 and WWW-Authenticate Bearer. `cp b0.json b2.json; MCP_REVIEW_CHECK_TOKEN= node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:18765/mcp --fail-on-incomplete --save-baseline b2.json --timeout 3000` gives exit 3, 'warning: --save-baseline: the check is partial (auth-required) ...' and then 'JSON report written to b2.json'. b2.json now has coverage auth-required and toolFingerprints null; the good-server baseline is gone.
findings.fix: Treat `values['fail-on-incomplete'] && partial` as unsaved too: 'the check is partial (<level>) and --fail-on-incomplete is set'. Optionally, without that flag, refuse to replace an existing baseline that has fingerprints with one that has none, unless a new --force-save-baseline is given.

votes.evidence: Reproduced against a local 127.0.0.1:18765 server that always answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate Bearer. The command `--fail-on-incomplete --save-baseline b2.json` exits 3. stderr shows the partial-check warning, then 'JSON report written to s/b2.json'. b2.json now has coverage.toolLevel auth-required and toolFingerprints null, and the good-server baseline is gone. The cause is in cli.ts:849: `unsaved` covers only snap.fatal and limits.stopped, which contradicts the A01-02 rationale for exit 3. One part of the claim is overstated: the documented GitLab recipe (ci.md:229-232) refreshes the baseline only through an after_script cp on CI_JOB_STATUS=success. That job would keep the baseline. The harm applies to direct `--save-baseline` refreshes, as in the ci.md:47-57 recipe.

findings.title: Listing-only run with --fail-on-drift always exits 1 with wrong advice
findings.claim: A listing-only run (--plugin-dir or --openai-manifest without a server) given --baseline and --fail-on-drift always exits 1. The advice 'fix this run (see the coverage line) before saving a baseline from it' cannot be followed: the coverage is fine and a listing-only run never lists tools. The listing-only guard at 597 rejects --active, --env and similar options as usage errors but not --fail-on-drift. A config file with failOnDrift and baseline that serves both server and listing runs therefore fails every listing run. The other way round, a listing-only baseline used for a server run is reported as 'the baseline run did not list every tool', when that run checked no server at all.
findings.repro: RAN: `node dist/cli.js --plugin-dir test/fixtures/listing/openai-invalid --baseline b0.json --fail-on-drift` gives exit 1 and stderr '--fail-on-drift: tool definitions not compared (this run did not list every tool: no server was checked (a listing-only run)); fix this run (see the coverage line) before saving a baseline from it'.
findings.fix: In the listing-only guard, make --fail-on-drift from the command line a usage error ('--fail-on-drift needs a <url> or --stdio target; a listing-only run lists no tools'). Drop failOnDrift that comes from the config file with a 'not used from' note, as is done for transport keys. For a baseline whose server.listingOnly is true, say 'the baseline is a listing-only report (no server was checked)'.

votes.evidence: With `--plugin-dir test/fixtures/listing/plugin-valid --baseline b0.json` the exit code is 0. Adding `--fail-on-drift` makes it exit 1 with stderr '--fail-on-drift: tool definitions not compared (this run did not list every tool: no server was checked (a listing-only run)); fix this run (see the coverage line) before saving a baseline from it'. The other 4 listing fixtures behave the same. The cause: drift.ts:85 returns that string for listing targets, :136 sets notComparedBy 'run', and cli.ts:830-835 then gives exit 1 with advice the user cannot follow. The listing-only guard at cli.ts:596-600 rejects --bearer, --header, --env, --cwd, --active, --active-auth and --tool-args, but not --fail-on-drift or --baseline. Round 3 A01-04 recommended 'Consider also rejecting --fail-on-drift in a listing-only run as a usage error'; that was not done.

findings.title: The baseline wildcard pass (A01-05 fix) is O(findings x wildcard entries) with polynomial regex backtracking
findings.claim: The 1.0.1 fallback matches a «redacted» baseline subject against any value. Each still-new finding is tested against every unused wildcard entry of the same rule with fresh regexes (Array.find), and is first checked with a lazy-quantifier regex per mark ('(?:[^"\\]|\\.)+?' in subjects, '.+?' in messages). That is quadratic in count, and polynomial in length per regex (O(L^k) for k marks in one string). The A01 perf work in round 3 made the main buckets linear, but this new path is not. Marks appear in baseline subjects or messages whenever a weak-tier value of 4+ characters (for example an --env value) is echoed in tool names or quoted text.
findings.repro: RAN (unit-level, node against dist/baseline.js): (a) n wildcard baseline entries {ruleId TOOL-011, tool '«redacted»_tool_i'} against n new findings that match none: 1000 took 3.7 s, 4000 took 25.7 s, 10000 took 73 s. (b) One entry whose tool is '«r»a«r»a«r»b' against one finding with a 4000-char tool 'aaaa…': 28.7 s; with 4 marks, a 200-char tool takes 1.4 s. (c) The message wordRe with 6 marks and a 300-char message: 12.4 s.
findings.fix: Replace the regexes with a linear glob matcher: split the subject on the mark, then match literal pieces with indexOf leftmost-first, which is correct for '*'-only globs, and check that no matched gap crosses a '"' in subjects. Index wildcard entries by the literal prefix and suffix of their subject (or by the (ruleId, tool-with-marks-stripped) shape) instead of scanning byRule lists, and cap the number of marks per entry (for example 8).

votes.evidence: In baseline.ts:162-180 every still-new finding runs `byRule.get(ruleId)?.find(...)` over all wildcard entries, in up to 4 passes (sameWording x forms). byRule is also built with an O(n^2) spread. Measured with dist/baseline.js: 1000 vs 1000 non-matching wildcard entries took 286 ms, 2000 took 1028 ms (about 4x, so quadratic). The subject regex joins marks with the lazy `(?:[^"\\]|\\.)+?`. One entry '«redacted»a«redacted»a«redacted»b' against a tool name of 1500 'a' characters took 1612 ms, which fits polynomial (about cubic) backtracking. One correction to the claim: the regexes are compiled once per entry, not anew per test. Real impact is low: it needs many «redacted» subjects in the baseline or long server-supplied names (capped at 16 KB).

findings.title: NUL bytes in config-file strings are not rejected: secrets echoed into the report, and a 'fatal' stack for paths
findings.claim: Command-line arguments cannot contain NUL, but JSON can ('\u0000'). An explicit --config whose env value or stdio argument contains a NUL reaches spawn. Node's error quotes the value with the NUL rendered as '\x00' ('Received ...'), so the whole-value redactor (which knows the raw NUL form) does not match it. The secret then appears in 'Could not connect' and in the SRV-003 finding of every format. A NUL in a path key (cwd, pluginDir, output) throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE from statSync, which prints as an internal 'fatal:' error with a stack trace (exit 3, 'please report it') instead of a usage error (exit 2).
findings.repro: RAN: c1.json = {"stdio":["node","test/fixtures/good-server.mjs","--api-key=S3cr\u0000etTokenValue123"]} prints 'Received '--api-key=S3cr\x00etTokenValue123'' in the text report and in SRV-003 (exit 3). c2.json with "env":{"API_KEY":"S3cr\u0000etTokenValue123"} does the same with 'options.env['API_KEY']'. c4.json with "cwd":"a\u0000b" gives 'fatal: TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE] ...' and a stack, exit 3.
findings.fix: In loadConfig, reject any string value (and list or map entry, and stdio/args/url) that contains U+0000, with ConfigError(`${where}: key "x" must not contain a NUL character (the value is not shown)`). As a safety net, also add the '\x00'-escaped form of each secret to the redactor forms in createRedactor.

votes.evidence: Reproduced. c1.json, with a stdio argument '--api-key=S3cr\u0000etTokenValue123', exits 3. The text report shows "Received '--api-key=S3cr\x00etTokenValue123'" both in 'Could not connect' and in SRV-003. c2.json puts the same value in env.API_KEY: the text report and `--format json` (2 hits each) contain 'etTokenValue123' through "options.env['API_KEY'] ... Received 'S3cr\x00etTokenValue123'". c4.json with cwd 'a\u0000b' prints 'fatal: TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE] ... without null bytes' and exits 3, not a usage error (exit 2). Low severity: this needs an explicit config file that contains a NUL.

improvements.title: Tally server notifications on stdio, legacy HTTP+SSE and the standalone GET stream
improvements.detail: Only the tracer's POST response bodies feed transport.notifications. The standalone Streamable HTTP GET stream is not read (isStream), and stdio and HTTP+SSE have no tracer, so SPEC-024 (needs: ['http']) never sees notifications/message there. RecordingTransport already sees every message (record() returns early on `method`). It could count method names, capped, and check log levels and the logging capability. That would extend SPEC-024's capability and level parts, which the 2025-11-25 logging page also states as MUSTs, to every transport. The 2026-07-28 logLevel-request part stays HTTP-only.

improvements.title: --connect-timeout to lift the 15 s HTTP handshake cap
improvements.detail: HTTP connect always waits min(--timeout, 15000) ms (connect.ts:408). Serverless and scale-to-zero servers (Cloud Run, Lambda, Fly machines) can take more than 15 s on a cold start. Today the check then fails with an unexplained timeout (see A02-04), and raising --timeout does not help. An option (or config key) with default 15000, as in 1.x, keeps the default behaviour and makes these servers checkable.

improvements.title: Proxy end-to-end diagnosis tests and a proxy line in --verbose
improvements.detail: test/p5a-proxy.test.ts covers routing for SOCKS5 and HTTP proxies but none of the failure diagnoses for SOCKS. A table test over UND_ERR_SOCKS5_* codes, HTTP 407 through plain forwarding, and the CONNECT 'Proxy response (407)' path would pin A02-02. A one-line `proxy: socks5://host:port via ALL_PROXY (NO_PROXY: ...)` in --verbose (credentials masked with proxyLabel) would let users see which route the run took.

improvements.title: Fix the proxy.ts comment on plain forwarding
improvements.detail: proxy.ts:109 says proxyTunnel:false sends http: targets as absolute-URI requests. undici does that only when the proxy itself is http:. With an https:// proxy URL, http: targets are still tunnelled with CONNECT, and with SOCKS nothing is forwarded. The comment and the diagnosis text ('allows CONNECT') should match what undici does.

findings.title: Each session-ending DELETE is awaited in turn for up to 5 s, so a server that does not answer DELETE adds 35 to 50 s per run
findings.claim: closeProbeSession awaits each raw-probe DELETE (preflight, 4 Origin probes, invalid-token) with timeoutMs min(timeoutMs, 5000). endSession awaits terminateSession with a 5000 ms withTimeout for the main connection and for every fresh connection (re-list, text-only, three clientInfo variants under --active). The answers are not evidence: ruleExchanges filters these DELETEs out. Yet a stateful server, gateway or WAF that holds DELETE open costs about 5 s each, one after another. The stop path already bounds the same request to 1.5 s in parallel (SESSION_END_TIMEOUT_MS).
findings.repro: RAN. A local stateful server (session id on initialize) that never answers DELETE (HANG=1 node hang-delete.mjs 18801), compared with the same server answering 200. `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:18801/mcp --quiet --timeout 10000` takes 37.6 s against 1.8 s. With --active it takes 52.0 s against 1.7 s. Server log: 7 DELETEs in the plain run, 10 with --active, each hanging.
findings.fix: Do not await the session closes inline. Start each DELETE (closeProbeSession and endSession), collect the promises, and at finishHttp (and on a stop) await them all at once, bounded by SESSION_END_TIMEOUT_MS (1.5 s). Or lower the per-DELETE wait to SESSION_END_TIMEOUT_MS and, after the first DELETE that gets no answer, send the rest without waiting (as the stall logic does for probes). Add a timing test with a DELETE-hanging fixture.

votes.evidence: Code at bc7090d: src/probe/network.ts:133-137 closeProbeSession awaits tracer.request DELETE with timeoutMs min(timeoutMs,5000). It is called after preflight (l.145), after each of the 4 Origin probes, which are awaited one after another in originProbes (l.195-200), and after invalidToken in src/probe/auth.ts:142. src/connect.ts:609-618 endSession awaits withTimeout(inner.terminateSession(), 5000). It is called from finishHttp (l.471) and from the finally of freshTools (l.594) for every fresh connection. No parallelism and no shorter bound on these paths. ruleExchanges (l.602-604) drops these DELETEs, so their answers are not evidence. endSessions/SESSION_END_TIMEOUT_MS=1500 with parallel fetch is used only on the stop/signal path. I found no guard that skips or shortens the regular-path DELETEs. Reproduced in a detached worktree (since removed) with a local stateful server that sets mcp-session-id on initialize: `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:18811/mcp --quiet --timeout 10000` took 37.6 s when DELETE hangs and 2.3 s when DELETE answers 200. The server logged 7 DELETEs in both runs, which matches 7 x 5 s. The --active run was not repeated; the code shows 3 more freshTools connections, each adding up to 5 s. Medium fits: it is not a correctness issue, but a run can be ~16x slower on servers or WAFs that hold DELETE open.

Read the code at bc7090d. In src/probe/network.ts:137, closeProbeSession awaits a single DELETE with timeoutMs Math.min(timeoutMs, 5000). In src/connect.ts:614, endSession awaits withTimeout(inner.terminateSession(), 5000), one connection after another. The stop path endSessions (connect.ts:667) runs its DELETEs in parallel with SESSION_END_TIMEOUT_MS=1500. ruleExchanges (connect.ts ~602) filters out the "(close session)" DELETEs and the sessionEnds DELETEs, so these answers are never evidence.

Repro: built the CLI in a detached worktree. Wrote a local stateful server that sets mcp-session-id on initialize and either answers DELETE with 200 or never answers it. Ran `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:PORT/mcp --quiet --timeout 10000`:
- DELETE answered: 2.7 s; with --active 2.2 s
- DELETE hanging: 36.8 s; with --active 53.0 s
The server logged 7 DELETEs in the plain run and 10 with --active, all sent one after another. This matches the claim (37.6/52.0 s).

The fix is easy: use the 1.5 s bound and/or run the DELETEs in parallel or without waiting for them. Medium perf severity is right: no wrong results, but up to about 50 s of extra wall time per run against a gateway or WAF that holds DELETE open. Worktree removed.

findings.title: Stop and Ctrl+C session DELETE does not follow a same-origin redirect, so the session stays open behind /mcp -> /mcp/
findings.claim: The new Q4-SESSION stop path (endSessions) sends DELETE to the URL as entered with redirect:'manual' and ignores the answer. trackSession records the URL passed to connectLegacyHttp, which is the URL as entered, not the redirect target. The SDK reached the session through fetchWithinOrigin, which follows 307/308 within the same origin, so the session lives at the target. With a /mcp -> 308 /mcp/ server, a run stopped by --max-duration, the byte budget or SIGINT/endAllNow sends `DELETE /mcp` and gets the 308, and the session is never ended. The regular path (endSession -> terminateSession) follows the redirect and works. So the 1.1.0 CHANGELOG claim that a stopped run 'ends the Streamable HTTP sessions the server issued' does not hold for exactly the slash-redirect case SRV-006 warns about.
findings.repro: RAN. A local server answers POST/DELETE /mcp with 308 Location:/mcp/. /mcp/ issues mcp-session-id on initialize and hangs on tools/list. Run `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:18741/mcp --max-duration 4000 --timeout 20000 --quiet`. Server log: `DELETE /mcp -> 308 sess-x9hexd`, and no DELETE ever reaches /mcp/. The same server without the redirect logs `SESSION DELETE sess-y8vubi`. Fixture: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-kali-packages/fae74d01-791a-469a-ab5f-90cdb063ebe5/scratchpad/a02/redir-session.mjs
findings.fix: In endSessions, follow 307/308 within the same origin (one or two hops, the SDK's isWithinOrigin rule, no userinfo added), still bounded by SESSION_END_TIMEOUT_MS. Alternatively, record the final URL in OpenSession: after connect, take the URL of the last 'sdk initialize' exchange that got 2xx, or use sameHostRedirect(url, pf). Add a case to test/r110-q4-session.test.ts with a 308 slash redirect.

votes.evidence: In connect.ts:303, trackSession stores the URL as entered (`url` passed to connectLegacyHttp at line 438, not `target`). endSessions (667-679) sends `fetch(s.url, {method:'DELETE', redirect:'manual'})` and ignores the answer. I re-ran this against bc7090d with the reviewer's redir-session.mjs on port 18841, using `--max-duration 4000 --timeout 20000`. Exit was 4 (stopped during listing). Server log: `DELETE /mcp/ sess-eqj46x` / `SESSION DELETE sess-eqj46x` comes from the raw probe session, which follows the target. The SDK session got only `DELETE /mcp -> 308 sess-c15yyc`, and no DELETE ever reached /mcp/ for it. So the CHANGELOG 1.1.0 Q4-SESSION claim fails in the same-origin 307/308 case. Impact is low because SRV-006 already warns about the redirect.

findings.title: SOCKS5 proxy failures get no proxy diagnosis, and the proxy-hop message calls a SOCKS proxy an 'HTTP proxy' that must allow CONNECT
findings.claim: PROXY_HOP and the 407 regex know only HTTP-proxy failures. undici's SOCKS5 agent fails with codes UND_ERR_SOCKS5_AUTH_FAILED, UND_ERR_SOCKS5_AUTH_REJECTED and UND_ERR_SOCKS5_REPLY_<n> (n=5: target refused through the proxy, 4: host unreachable, 2: not allowed by ruleset). These are not in PROXY_HOP, so describeCause falls through to `fetch failed (UND_ERR_SOCKS5_AUTH_FAILED)` with kind 'other', no hint and no proxy named. When a SOCKS proxy is down, the message reads 'through the HTTP proxy socks5://... allows CONNECT ... check HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY', even though ALL_PROXY set it and SOCKS uses no CONNECT. SOCKS5 support was added deliberately (README, proxy.ts SUPPORTED), so its failure path should be diagnosed as well as the HTTP-proxy one.
findings.repro: RAN against local fixtures. (1) A SOCKS5 server that rejects username/password: `ALL_PROXY='socks5://alice:s3cretPW@127.0.0.1:18750' node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:18742/mcp` -> `Result: FAIL (could not connect: fetch failed (UND_ERR_SOCKS5_AUTH_FAILED))`, JSON coverage.diagnosis {kind:'other', summary:'fetch failed (UND_ERR_SOCKS5_AUTH_FAILED)'}. No credential leak: 0 matches for the user or password in --format json --verbose. (2) A working SOCKS5 forwarder to a closed port gives `fetch failed (UND_ERR_SOCKS5_REPLY_5)`, while the same target without the proxy gives the proper 'connection refused by 127.0.0.1:18799 (ECONNREFUSED)'. (3) `ALL_PROXY=socks5://127.0.0.1:18759` (nothing listening) gives 'cannot reach ... through the HTTP proxy socks5://127.0.0.1:18759 (ECONNREFUSED); check HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY: ... allows CONNECT'.
findings.fix: In describeCause, when proxyForUrl(url) is a socks5 or socks URL: treat /^UND_ERR_SOCKS5_/ as a proxy hop. Map AUTH_FAILED and AUTH_REJECTED to a 'proxy auth' diagnosis (credentials in the socks5://user:pass@ URL). Map REPLY_5 to 'the SOCKS proxy could not connect to host:port (refused)', REPLY_4 and REPLY_3 to unreachable, and REPLY_2 to 'not allowed by the proxy's rules'. Name the proxy kind from the scheme ('SOCKS5 proxy' or 'HTTP proxy'). Name the variable that supplied it (HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY or ALL_PROXY, as installProxy already works out). Say 'allows CONNECT' only for an http(s) proxy with an https target. Add cases to test/p5a-proxy.test.ts, whose SOCKS5 fixture already exists.

votes.evidence: diagnose.ts:25 PROXY_HOP has no UND_ERR_SOCKS5_* codes. The proxy summary at 52-53 is hard-coded as 'through the HTTP proxy ... allows CONNECT ... check HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY'. Re-ran: (1) `ALL_PROXY=socks5://127.0.0.1:18859` with nothing listening gives 'cannot reach 127.0.0.1:18842 through the HTTP proxy socks5://127.0.0.1:18859 (ECONNREFUSED); check HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY: ... allows CONNECT'. (2) socks-reject.mjs with `socks5://alice:pw@...` gives 'Could not connect: fetch failed (UND_ERR_SOCKS5_AUTH_FAILED)' with the generic SRV-003 fix line and no proxy named. CHANGELOG 1.1.0 already fixed the same 'HTTP proxy' wording for SOCKS in the TLS check message, so the connect diagnosis is inconsistent with it. Not covered in round 3.

findings.title: A handshake that fails on a redirect gets the raw SDK text and no hint to use the final URL
findings.claim: describeHttpFailure has no 3xx branch. When the server answers the initialize POST with 301, 302 or 303 (which the SDK never follows for a POST), or with a cross-origin 307/308, the user sees `HTTP 301: Streamable HTTP error: Error POSTing to endpoint: Redirect to http://127.0.0.1:18771/mcp/ not followed (redirectPolicy: 'same-origin')`. That is SDK-internal wording ('redirectPolicy'). The fix line is the generic SRV-003 one. Nothing says that MCP clients do not re-send a POST after 301/302/303, or suggests running the check against the final URL. The preflight already holds the Location (sameHostRedirect) and could name it.
findings.repro: RAN. A server answers /mcp with 301 Location:/mcp/ and serves Streamable HTTP at /mcp/ (`CODE=301 node redir-code.mjs 18771`). Run `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:18771/mcp --timeout 5000`. Output: `Could not connect: HTTP 301: Streamable HTTP error: Error POSTing to endpoint: Redirect to http://127.0.0.1:18771/mcp/ not followed (redirectPolicy: 'same-origin')`, with the generic 'fix  Check the URL ...' line.
findings.fix: Add a redirect case to describeHttpFailure, given the preflight's Location (conn.headers.location or snap.transport.preflight). For 301/302/303: summary 'HTTP 301: the server redirects the POST to <target>; MCP clients do not re-send a POST after 301/302/303', hint 'register and check <target> (mcp-review-check <target>), or redirect with 307/308'. For a cross-origin or https->http 307/308: say clients do not follow a redirect to another origin. Use kind 'http', so the JSON enum does not change. Strip the '(redirectPolicy: ...)' suffix in cleanErrorMessage.

votes.evidence: Re-ran `CODE=301 node redir-code.mjs 18871` and `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:18871/mcp --timeout 5000`. The connect line does show the raw SDK text ('... not followed (redirectPolicy: 'same-origin')') with the generic SRV-003 fix. But the same report then prints `! SRV-006 [claude] server: POST redirects (301) to http://127.0.0.1:18871/mcp/; register the final URL` with 'fix  Register the final URL, or serve MCP directly at the entered URL.' So the user already gets the final URL and the next step. The finding's central claim that nothing names the Location or suggests the final URL is false. Only cosmetic: the SDK wording 'redirectPolicy' in the summary.

findings.title: An initialize timeout reads only 'MCP error -32001: Request timed out', without the request or the wait
findings.claim: When a server accepts the connection but never answers initialize, the fatal message and coverage reason are the SDK's bare `MCP error -32001: Request timed out`. They do not say it was initialize, how long the check waited, or that HTTP connect waits min(--timeout, 15000) ms whatever --timeout is set to. A user with a slow cold-start server who raises --timeout to 60000 still fails at 15 s with the same unexplained message. describeHttpFailure gets status undefined and no cause, so it returns the message with no hint.
findings.repro: RAN. A local HTTP server answers the raw probes with 404 and never answers the SDK initialize (hang-init.mjs). Run `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:18781/mcp --timeout 3000`. Output: `Could not connect: MCP error -32001: Request timed out`, after 4.0 s. The stdio hang at initialize shows the same text plus stderr.
findings.fix: In connectLegacyHttp and connectStdio, rewrite a timeout (McpError -32001, or 'timed out after') to 'initialize got no answer within <connectTimeout> ms'. For HTTP add the hint: 'the server accepted the connection but did not answer; HTTP connect waits min(--timeout, 15000) ms; a cold-starting server may need a warm-up request first'. Map it to the existing kind 'timeout' in the diagnosis.

votes.evidence: connect.ts:408 `connectTimeout = Math.min(timeoutMs, 15000)` is passed to connectLegacyHttp (438). The SDK error message is used verbatim (310), and describeHttpFailure's fallback (164) returns it with no hint. I found no mention of the 15 s cap in the README at bc7090d. Re-ran hang-init.mjs on port 18882 with `--timeout 60000`: exit 3 after 16 s, with 'Could not connect: MCP error -32001: Request timed out' and the generic SRV-003 fix. It does not mention initialize, the wait, or the cap. A UX finding, low as reported.

areas.name: probes
areas.coverage: Read at bc7090d in a detached worktree (npm ci --ignore-scripts, npm run build; removed afterwards, fixture servers stopped): src/probe/active.ts, auth.ts, network.ts and wire.ts in full. Also read the probe wiring in src/connect.ts:400-600 (buildHttp, probeAuth, runWireProbes and runActive calls, freshTools), ModernClient.request and mcpNameOf in src/protocol/modern.ts, tokenize in src/rules/util/text.ts, the lexicon, src/rules/runtime.ts RT-001..006, cli.ts unusedToolArgs and readToolArgs, docs/guide/privacy-and-requests.md, CHANGELOG 1.0.1 and 1.1.0, the round 3 FINDINGS and REMEDIATION (A03 items and improvements), and the round 1 refuted SSRF items F026/F140 (not re-reported). Spec pages fetched: 2026-07-28 streamable-http, transports overview, subscriptions. Ran: buildSnapshot with --active against good-server.mjs and bad-server.mjs (stdio); hasWriteVerb over about 130 names plus tokenize edge cases; CLI --active against a spec-validating modern-only server I wrote (A03-01, A03-03); CLI --bearer --active-auth against a legacy server whose tools/list returns 401 (A03-02); the --tool-args warning against bad-server (A03-04); --verbose request list of a modern-only run. Not done: TLS-check behaviour against a real certificate or an https fixture; SSE-mode Origin probes against a legacy HTTP+SSE server; a --max-duration stop during the auth probe or --active-auth (the improvement is from the code only); the tasks/get parameter shape against the tasks extension page; vitest files were not run.

improvements.title: Wider write-verb coverage and token splitting in the --active name filter
improvements.detail: These names, all annotated readOnlyHint: true, still pass hasWriteVerb at 1.1.0 (ran it against dist/probe/active.js): upsert_*, append_*, restore_*, migrate_*, unpublish_*, charge_card, sign, vote, follow/unfollow, retweet, launch, scale, resize, mount/unmount, format_disk, encrypt/decrypt, rotate_key, configure, store, attach/detach, broadcast, alert, escalate, acknowledge, resolve_incident ('resolve' is a READ verb). tokenize splits only on _-./: and whitespace, so read+delete, read&delete and a zero-width-space join (get​delete) are one token. NFKC folding and splitting on any non-alphanumeric character would close those cases. Checking annotations.title and title with the same filter would add defence in depth. Calling fewer tools is patch-safe, as A03-01 of round 3 was.

improvements.title: An explicit --active allowlist (--active-tools <name|glob>) and a dry-run listing of the planned calls
improvements.detail: Today the only way to narrow --active is to rely on annotations and the name heuristic. An allowlist, together with a mode that prints which tools would be called with which synthesized arguments without sending anything, would let a reviewer approve the side effects before running against a production server. This matches the tool's read-only, side-effect-free promise.

improvements.title: Publish clientInfo variants as they finish
improvements.detail: runActive assigns result.clientInfoVariants only after all three fresh connections (active.ts:251-258). A --max-duration stop during the third listing loses the two that finished. Write into ctx.into after each variant, as the calls already are.

improvements.title: Better argument synthesis for common generator shapes, and a coverage note when synthetic calls fail validation
improvements.detail: placeholder() ignores prefixItems (pydantic Tuple[float,float] becomes prefixItems + minItems) and returns strings for each item. It also ignores required/properties inside allOf when a sibling type: 'object' exists, and a top-level $ref or allOf in inputSchema (synthesizeArgs calls objectPlaceholder directly). Synthetic calls that fail only because of the linter's arguments hide RT-004 and RT-006. Support prefixItems, merge allOf object branches and resolve a root $ref. In the report, say how many synthetic calls returned a validation error and suggest --tool-args for those tools.

improvements.title: Report the request count per run
improvements.detail: The privacy guide states '20 to 40 requests'. A JSON field such as limits.requests ({total, byLabel}) and a one-line stderr summary would back that claim for each run and make duplicate probing visible (see A03-02).

improvements.title: Print the DCR notice even when the run stops after registration
improvements.detail: This is related to the known round-3 improvement 'publish partial auth-probe results'. Since 1.1.0 the DCR client_id notice depends on snap.authProbe, which is assigned only after the whole probe returns. A --max-duration stop between the DCR POST and the end of /authorize and /token loses the only record of the client that was created. Recording the DCR exchange into the snapshot right away would keep the A03-03 promise. This was read from the code, not run.

findings.line: 211 (call(), modern path); header building in src/protocol/modern.ts:96-102
findings.title: --active tools/call on a 2026-07-28 server leaves out the Mcp-Param-* headers for x-mcp-header parameters, so a conforming server rejects the call and RT-003 reports a false positive
findings.claim: For a modern-only server, runActive sends tools/call through ModernClient.request. That method sets only Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name. The streamable-http page of 2026-07-28 says clients MUST mirror x-mcp-header parameters into Mcp-Param-{Name}, and servers MUST reject a request with 400 / -32020 HeaderMismatch when the value is in the body but the header is missing. As a result: (1) the synthetic or valid call to any tool with an x-mcp-header parameter that has a value gets -32020, so RT-004 and RT-006 never see a result (lost coverage); (2) the invalid-type call keeps the other synthetic arguments, gets -32020 too, and RT-003 (spec: warning) reports 'invalid-type input returned a JSON-RPC error instead of isError' against a compliant server. Dual-era servers are not affected because they go through the legacy SDK client.
findings.repro: Ran it: a standalone 2026-07-28 server (scratchpad a03-modern-hdr.mjs on 127.0.0.1:38431) with tool get_forecast {region: string with x-mcp-header 'Region', city}, both required, readOnlyHint true. It validates headers as the spec requires. `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:38431/mcp --active --format json` gave `RT-003 warning get_forecast invalid-type input returned a JSON-RPC error instead of isError`, and the server logged `REJECT missing Mcp-Param-Region for get_forecast args={"region":"mcp-review-check",...}` for both the synthetic and the invalid-type call.
findings.fix: In active.ts call(), for the modern path, walk the tool's inputSchema along the plain properties chain (as TOOL-021 does) and pass headers Mcp-Param-{x-mcp-header} built from the argument values: string as is, integer as decimal, boolean lowercase, and the =?base64?…?= form for non-ASCII, control characters, leading or trailing whitespace, or a value that looks like the sentinel. Omit the header for null or absent values. Add an extraHeaders option to ModernRequestOptions. Skip tools that TOOL-021 finds invalid, because a client drops them. As a safety net, RT-003 should not count a -32020 error as 'JSON-RPC error instead of isError'. This is a patch: it removes a false positive.

votes.evidence: I read the code at bc7090d. In src/protocol/modern.ts, ModernClient.request builds only content-type, accept, mcp-protocol-version, mcp-method and mcp-name (from params.name/uri via mcpNameOf), plus the user's own headers. `git grep -i "mcp-param"` finds nothing in src/ or test/, so x-mcp-header parameters are never mirrored into Mcp-Param-* headers anywhere. x-mcp-header shows up only in the static rules TOOL-021/022 (src/rules/schema.ts), and TOOL-021's rationale itself says "Streamable HTTP clients mirror x-mcp-header parameters into HTTP headers". In src/probe/active.ts, call() goes to ctx.modern!.request('tools/call', {name, arguments}) whenever ctx.client is unset. connect.ts:557-558 passes `modern: conn.ok ? undefined : modern`, so only modern-only servers take this path; dual-era servers use the legacy SDK client, as the finding says. runActive sends the synthetic/valid call, and then the invalid-type call as `{...args, [first]: wrong}`, which keeps the synthetic value of the header-bound parameter. The invalid-missing call ({}) carries no value and is not affected. RT-003 (src/rules/runtime.ts:72-78) is `isInvalid(c) && c.jsonRpcError !== undefined` with no exclusion for -32020..-32022. That is unlike SPEC rules in src/rules/spec.ts:219, which explicitly skip header rejections of their own probes. So a -32020 HeaderMismatch from a conforming server becomes 'invalid-type input returned a JSON-RPC error instead of isError'. RT-004 and RT-006 look only at successful results, so they lose coverage for that tool. I found no guard elsewhere. I did not re-run the repro, but the code path matches the reported output exactly. Severity medium: a false-positive warning plus lost coverage, limited to modern-only servers with x-mcp-header tools under --active.

Code at bc7090d: src/protocol/modern.ts request() sets only content-type, accept, mcp-protocol-version, mcp-method and mcp-name. grep shows no 'Mcp-Param' or 'mcp-param' anywhere in src/protocol or src/probe; the only x-mcp-header code is the TOOL-021/022 lint rules in src/rules/schema.ts. On the modern path, src/probe/active.ts call() sends tools/call through ctx.modern.request('tools/call', params, ...) with no extra headers.

Spec (fetched from modelcontextprotocol.io 2026-07-28 streamable-http): clients MUST mirror x-mcp-header values into Mcp-Param-{Name}. The scenario table says 'Client omits header but value is in body: Non-conforming client / Server MUST reject the request'. Servers MUST reply 400 with -32020 HeaderMismatch.

Run: I made a detached worktree at bc7090d, ran npm ci and the build, and started the scratchpad a03-modern-hdr.mjs server on 127.0.0.1:38477. It is a modern-only server that validates headers per the spec, with get_forecast{region (x-mcp-header Region), city} marked readOnly. Then I ran `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:38477/mcp --active --format json`. The server logged 'REJECT missing Mcp-Param-Region for get_forecast' twice: once for the synthetic call (region:"mcp-review-check") and once for the invalid-type call (region:12345). The CLI output contained 'RT-003 warning get_forecast: invalid-type input returned a JSON-RPC error instead of isError', which is a false positive against a compliant server. The synthetic and valid calls also produced no result, so the result-based RT checks lost coverage.

Side observation, a separate issue: the same run gave RT-003 for the non-ASCII tool 'météo'. The client sent Mcp-Name percent-encoded ("m%C3%A9t%C3%A9o") instead of the Base64 sentinel the spec requires, so the server rejected it. That is a different root cause and is not part of A03-01.

Severity is medium: the bug yields a false-positive warning plus lost --active coverage, only on modern-only servers that use x-mcp-header. Dual-era servers are not affected because they use the legacy SDK client. The worktree has been removed.

findings.line: 498 (if (trigger) await probeAuth()) and 517-519 (second probeAuth after tools/list 401); src/probe/auth.ts:165,175-188
findings.title: The auth probe can run twice in one run; with --active-auth that registers two DCR clients, and only the second client_id is reported
findings.claim: probeAuth runs once when the unauthenticated preflight gets 401, even when credentials are supplied. It runs a second time when the authenticated tools/list later gets 401 (an expired token, or a server that accepts any bearer for initialize). Each run repeats all PRM and AS GETs plus timing samples, the invalid-token probe, the AS TLS handshakes (pushed twice into transport.tls) and, with --active-auth, the whole active sequence: a second DCR registration, 3 more /authorize GETs and 2 more /token POSTs. snap.authProbe is overwritten, so dcrClientNotice and authProbe.active.clientId name only the second client. The first DCR client is left on the user's authorization server and never disclosed, which undoes the 1.0.1/1.1.0 A03-03 fix ('so you can delete it'). The request count also goes beyond what privacy-and-requests.md describes.
findings.repro: Ran it: scratchpad a03-auth2.mjs on 127.0.0.1:38432 is a stateless 2025-11-25 server. initialize returns 401 without a bearer and 200 with any bearer; tools/list returns 401 with a resource_metadata challenge; it also serves PRM/AS metadata with registration_endpoint. `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:38432/mcp --bearer sometoken-abcdef --active-auth --format json`. stderr printed only `registered DCR client client_id=client-2`. Server counters: POST /register 2, GET /authorize 6, POST /token 4, GET PRM 6, GET AS metadata 6.
findings.fix: Run the auth probe at most once per run. If it already ran from the preflight trigger, the tools/list 401 path should only call rejected() and reuse snap.authProbe (or, if the second challenge differs, re-read just the challenge without the metadata, TLS and --active-auth steps). Separately, collect every DCR exchange and print one notice per accepted registration, so no client is left undisclosed. Also dedupe transport.tls by host and role. This is a patch.

votes.evidence: Read src/connect.ts and src/probe/auth.ts at bc7090d with git show. Line 434 sets `trigger = 'preflight-401'` whenever the unauthenticated preflight (authPf) gets 401. Credentials do not change this. Line 497 runs `if (trigger) await probeAuth();` unconditionally, so a run with --bearer still probes once. If the authenticated connect then succeeds (conn.ok, so authFailed is false), the code goes on to listEverything. A 401 on tools/list (lines 514-519) calls rejected(), where `trigger ??=` keeps 'preflight-401', and then calls `await probeAuth()` again. Nothing guards against this: there is no check of snap.authProbe and no flag recording that the probe already ran. probeAuth (lines 483-495) calls runAuthProbe again, which repeats the PRM/AS fetches, the invalid-token probe and the DNS lookups. With activeAuth it also repeats activeAuth() (auth.ts:165), which POSTs registration_endpoint (DCR) again plus the /authorize GETs and /token POSTs. probeAuth then overwrites `snap.authProbe = probe` and pushes the AS TLS observations into `tls` a second time. So authProbe.active.clientId, and the DCR notice built from it, name only the second client, and the first registered client is never reported. The second run is also not limited to a token rejected outright on initialize: any server that accepts any bearer for initialize and checks it only on tools/list, or an expired token, reaches it. I did not re-run it; the code path matches the submitted repro exactly (POST /register twice, only client-2 printed). Medium severity is right: it leaves an undisclosed artifact on the user's authorization server, partly reverses the earlier "so you can delete it" disclosure fix, and sends more requests than the documented count. It is not a correctness error in the findings.

Read bc7090d src/connect.ts: trigger is set from the unauthenticated preflight (authPf.status===401 -> 'preflight-401') whether or not credentials are given. Line 498 `if (trigger) await probeAuth()` runs, then at 517-519 a tools/list 401 calls rejected() (trigger ??= keeps the old trigger) and `await probeAuth()` again. probeAuth overwrites snap.authProbe and pushes AS TLS results to tls again. runAuthProbe (auth.ts:165) calls activeAuth each time, and that registers a new DCR client every run. I built the CLI in a detached worktree and ran the reviewer's fixture on 127.0.0.1:38461: `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:38461/mcp --bearer sometoken-abcdef --active-auth --format json`. stderr reported only `registered DCR client client_id=client-2`, and JSON authProbe.active.clientId=client-2. Server counters: POST /register 2, GET /authorize 6, POST /token 4, GET PRM 6, GET AS metadata 6. The first DCR client (client-1) is never disclosed, so the A03-03 'so you can delete it' notice is defeated, and the request count is double what the docs describe. Trigger conditions: preflight 401, then the authenticated initialize succeeds, then tools/list gets 401 (expired token, scope step-up, or lazy token validation). That is plausible but not the common path, so medium is right. Worktree removed.

findings.line: 57-64 (mcpNameOf), used by active.ts:211 and the modern resources/read path
findings.title: Mcp-Name is percent-encoded instead of the spec's =?base64?…?= form, so active calls to non-ASCII tool names are rejected with HeaderMismatch
findings.claim: mcpNameOf replaces characters outside visible ASCII with encodeURIComponent output. The 2026-07-28 streamable-http page says that a name or URI outside the safe set (non-ASCII, control characters, leading or trailing whitespace, or a value matching the sentinel) MUST be sent as `=?base64?…?=`, and that servers MUST decode it before comparing it with the body. A conforming server compares 'm%C3%A9t%C3%A9o' with 'météo' and returns 400 -32020. The synthetic call for that tool then gets no result, and its invalid-missing and invalid-type calls produce false RT-003 warnings. The same applies to modern resources/read of a UI resource whose URI is non-ASCII. Tool names outside [A-Za-z0-9_.-] are only a SHOULD violation, so the tool still has to handle them. This file belongs to area A02; it is listed here because --active is the main consumer.
findings.repro: Ran it: same server as A03-01, with tool 'météo' (readOnlyHint true). The server logged `REJECT Mcp-Name "m%C3%A9t%C3%A9o" for météo` three times, and the report showed `RT-003 warning météo invalid-missing input returned a JSON-RPC error instead of isError` and `... invalid-type ...`.
findings.fix: Encode the value as `=?base64?${Buffer.from(v,'utf8').toString('base64')}?=` when it has characters outside 0x20-0x7E or a tab, has leading or trailing whitespace, or matches /^=\?base64\?.*\?=$/. Otherwise send it unchanged. Share the encoder with the Mcp-Param-* headers from A03-01. This is a patch.

votes.evidence: At bc7090d, src/protocol/modern.ts:58-64 (mcpNameOf) uses `v.replace(/[^\x20-\x7E]/gu, encodeURIComponent)`, which percent-encodes non-ASCII. It sends leading/trailing whitespace and values matching the sentinel unchanged. modern.ts:101 uses it for every tools/call and resources/read. I fetched the live 2026-07-28 streamable-http page (Value Encoding section). It says that if a name or URI cannot be represented as plain ASCII, it is carried as `Mcp-Name: =?base64?{Base64EncodedValue}?=`. It also says 'servers MUST decode an encoded Mcp-Name ... before comparing it to the corresponding request body value', and Server Validation says a mismatch MUST get 400 / -32020. A conforming server therefore compares 'm%C3%A9t%C3%A9o' with 'météo' and rejects the call. In src/probe/active.ts:200-214, call() on the modern path keeps r.error as jsonRpcError. RT-003 (src/rules/runtime.ts:77) flags any invalid-missing or invalid-type call that has jsonRpcError !== undefined and does not exclude -32020. The false RT-003 warnings follow directly from that, and the synthetic or valid call returns no result. Leading/trailing whitespace and sentinel-matching names are also sent raw, which goes against the same MUST. I verified this by reading the code and the spec; I did not re-run the reported repro.

findings.title: The --tool-args 'not used' warning blames readOnlyHint for tools that are annotated read-only, and says 'past the cap' for duplicate names
findings.claim: isSafeToCall is false in three cases: readOnlyHint is not true, destructiveHint is true, or the name contains a write verb. The warning always says 'the tool is not read-only (readOnlyHint: true)'. A tool annotated readOnlyHint: true that the name filter skipped (delete_x) or that is also destructiveHint: true (archive_items) therefore gets a message that contradicts its own annotations. The user cannot tell that the 1.0.1 name filter caused the skip, or how to get the call made. Separately, a name listed twice where one entry is unsafe passes isSafeToCall on the first entry and gets 'the tool was past the cap on --active calls'. That reason is wrong too: callableTools rejected it for the duplicate. A --max-duration stop before the call gets the same wrong 'cap' reason. The duplicate and stop cases were read from the code, not run.
findings.repro: Ran it: `echo '{"delete_x":{},"archive_items":{}}' > a.json; node dist/cli.js --stdio "node test/fixtures/bad-server.mjs" --active --tool-args a.json --format json` printed `--tool-args entry "delete_x" was not used: the tool is not read-only (readOnlyHint: true)`, although bad-server.mjs:80 annotates delete_x with readOnlyHint: true, destructiveHint: false.
findings.fix: Have active.ts export a function that returns the skip reason ('readOnlyHint is not true', 'destructiveHint is true', 'the name contains the write verb "delete"', 'the name is listed more than once and not every entry is read-only'), plus 'the run stopped before this call' when limits.stopped is set. Use it in unusedToolArgs. This is a patch (message text only).

votes.evidence: At bc7090d, src/cli.ts unusedToolArgs, the line that builds `why`, uses one string for every `!isSafeToCall(tool)` case: 'the tool is not read-only (readOnlyHint: true), so --active does not call it'. In src/probe/active.ts:61-64, isSafeToCall is also false when destructiveHint is true or when hasWriteVerb(name) matches. test/fixtures/bad-server.mjs annotates delete_x with `readOnlyHint: true, destructiveHint: false`, so it is skipped only by the name filter, and the message contradicts its own annotation. snap.tools.find returns only the first entry with that name. If that entry is safe and a duplicate is not, callableTools (active.ts:222-229, `entries.every(isSafeToCall)`) drops the tool, and the message falls through to the 'past the cap' reason. A --max-duration stop (calls made so far are kept via ctx.into) also ends in that 'cap' branch. Low severity: the warning text is wrong, the behaviour is not. I checked this by reading the code and did not run it.

areas.name: protocol, auth, server and runtime rules and the engine
areas.coverage: Read at bc7090d in a detached worktree (npm ci --ignore-scripts and npm run build; the worktree is removed). Read in full: src/rules/engine.ts, spec.ts, auth.ts, server.ts and runtime.ts. Read in part: src/probe/network.ts (lookupHost, preflight), src/probe/auth.ts (activeAuth), src/probe/wire.ts (the modern probes), src/protocol/trace.ts (noteNotifications, abortAfterHeaders), src/connect.ts (readUiResources, buildHttp, probe wiring), src/rules/util/obs.ts, util/ui.ts, util/access.ts and util/net.ts (isLocalTarget). Checked against the round-1 and round-3 FINDINGS and REMEDIATION and the CHANGELOG sections for 1.0.1 and 1.1.0; none of the findings above are listed there. improvements.title: Record stdio server notifications so SPEC-024 also runs for stdio servers
improvements.detail: Only the HTTP tracer tallies notifications/message (src/protocol/trace.ts noteNotifications), so SPEC-024 has needs ['http'] and every stdio server gets 'stdio target'. The 2025-11-25 logging page also says servers that emit log notifications MUST declare the logging capability. Tally the notifications that arrive in the stdio transport's onmessage (null-prototype table, same cap) and drop the 'http' need. The 'unrequested' check applies to 2026-07-28 requests only.

improvements.title: Check that a 403 insufficient_scope challenge carries resource_metadata
improvements.detail: The 2026-07-28 runtime-insufficient-scope section lists resource_metadata as a parameter of the 403 challenge 'for consistency with 401 responses'. AUTH-003 already parses the 403 challenge but checks only error= and scope=. Add a spec info or warning when resource_metadata is missing (it is a SHOULD).

improvements.title: An explicit 'server answered' need instead of the engine's catch-all skip
improvements.detail: Today the engine decides 'found nothing because it saw nothing' after the rule runs, from the URL_ONLY allowlist plus fatal or connect-failed (and, per A04-03, auth-required). A declared need, for example 'handshake' (initializeRaw or discoverRaw present), on SPEC-002/008/016..023 and SRV-011..015 would give correct skip reasons up front. It would also stop findings that rules emit from partial data (such as a preflight) from slipping through, and keep the URL_ONLY list from drifting as rules are added.

improvements.title: Show 'inconclusive' active-auth results in the report when no client_id was obtained
improvements.detail: When --active-auth cannot register (no registration_endpoint, as with CIMD-only or pre-registered authorization servers, or a DCR failure), AUTH-020 and AUTH-021 probe with a placeholder client_id. Tell the user once (stderr notice or an AUTH-019 info) that the /authorize and /token checks ran with a placeholder client and that their results only show whether the endpoint parses the request. As a follow-up, accept --client-id <id> so the redirect check is meaningful for pre-registered or CIMD setups.

improvements.title: Name the resolver used in SRV-004 messages and record the resolv.conf servers
improvements.detail: SRV-004 says '(system resolver)' and 'public DNS', but dns.resolve4 uses the resolv.conf servers, which may be split-horizon corporate DNS. Recording which resolver answered (dns.getServers()) in the DnsResult and showing it in the message would let users tell an environment problem from a real DNS defect. This complements A04-02.

findings.title: AUTH-020 turns any HTTP 400 from /authorize into a Claude error saying redirect_uri was rejected, even when the bogus client_id is the real cause
findings.claim: The active probe sends client_id='mcp-review-check' whenever no DCR client was registered: a CIMD-only or pre-registered authorization server, or a DCR attempt that failed. Such an authorization server answers /authorize with 400 invalid_client (or invalid_request, for example when scope is required). AUTH-020 treats `ex.status === 400` alone as 'rejected redirect_uri' and gives a Claude error for each of the three callbacks, so the run exits 1. The status code alone is a heuristic, and the project's severity principle caps heuristics at warning.
findings.repro: Ran it. Started a loopback OAuth stub: PRM, RFC 8414 metadata with client_id_metadata_document_supported=true and no registration_endpoint, and /authorize -> 400 {"error":"invalid_client"}. Ran `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:47811/mcp --active-auth --format json`. Result: exit 1 with three `AUTH-020 error claude /authorize rejected redirect_uri ... (400)` findings (http://127.0.0.1:3118/callback, http://localhost:3118/callback, https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback).
findings.fix: Count a 400 as a redirect rejection only when the body names the redirect (REDIRECT_REJECTED, or an error/error_description that mentions redirect). For a 400 whose OAuth error is invalid_client, unauthorized_client or invalid_request with no redirect wording, or for any 400 when no DCR client_id was obtained (authProbe.active.clientId is missing), report an info: 'inconclusive: /authorize refused the probe's client_id (...); redirect_uri not verified'. This lowers a severity, so it fits a patch release.

votes.evidence:
I confirmed this by reading the code at bc7090d. I did not build it or re-run the repro, because the code path is clear on its own.

1. Probe, src/probe/auth.ts:175-203. DCR is attempted only when meta.registration_endpoint exists. out.clientId is set only if the DCR response contains a client_id. Otherwise `const clientId = out.clientId ?? 'mcp-review-check'` (line 189), and that placeholder is sent as client_id to /authorize for all three CALLBACKS. The /authorize probe has no guard that skips it when no client was registered.

2. Rule, src/rules/auth.ts:556-563. The condition `if (ex.status === 400 || REDIRECT_REJECTED.test(body) || ...)` reports a 400 alone as `/authorize rejected redirect_uri ${redirect} (${ex.status})`. No severity is set on the finding, so it takes the rule default `{ claude: 'error' }`. The rule never checks snap.authProbe.active.clientId and never reads the OAuth error code: an invalid_client or invalid_request body still counts. The only other references to AUTH-020 are its rule registration (line 605) and the spec, so nothing else filters it.

3. Consequence. A CIMD-only or pre-registered AS correctly answers an unknown, non-URL client_id with 400 invalid_client. RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 says the AS must not redirect when the client_id is invalid. That gives three claude errors and exit 1, yet Claude would send its CIMD URL as client_id and pass. CIMD is the path the tool itself recommends, since AUTH-0xx says DCR is deprecated for new servers.

4. History and spec. docs/design/spec.md:1021 says "A 400, or an error body mentioning redirect_uri → error", so the 400-only branch matches the spec. But spec.md:1016 ("Store the client_id for AUTH-020") assumes a DCR client_id exists, and the spec does not cover the placeholder case. Round-3 F038 (CHANGELOG 1.0.1/1.1.0) only fixed the false positive for a login page containing redirect_uri. This 400-without-a-real-client case is new and was not reported before.

5. Severity principle. A bare 400 does not deterministically point to redirect_uri as the cause, so an error-level verdict breaks the "heuristic ≤ warning" rule.

Severity: medium. It only runs with opt-in --active-auth, but in that mode it falsely BLOCKS a correctly configured CIMD-only or pre-registered AS (exit 1).

Suggested fix: when out.clientId is absent, skip the check or downgrade to info/warning. Also ignore an error body whose code is invalid_client, unauthorized_client or invalid_scope unless it mentions redirect_uri.

Code at bc7090d: src/probe/auth.ts activeAuth uses `clientId = out.clientId ?? 'mcp-review-check'` when there is no registration_endpoint or the DCR request fails. src/rules/auth.ts AUTH_020 has the condition `if (ex.status === 400 || REDIRECT_REJECTED.test(body) || ...)`. A 400 status alone is enough to emit the rule's default Claude error "/authorize rejected redirect_uri ...". The error body is never checked. Repro: I built bc7090d in a detached worktree and ran a loopback stub on 127.0.0.1:47811. The stub served PRM and RFC 8414 metadata with client_id_metadata_document_supported=true and no registration_endpoint. Its /authorize answered 400 {"error":"invalid_client"}. Running `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:47811/mcp --active-auth --format json` exited 1. The only error findings were three AUTH-020 errors: "/authorize rejected redirect_uri http://127.0.0.1:3118/callback (400)", the same for localhost:3118, and the same for https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback. The real cause is the made-up client_id 'mcp-review-check', which a CIMD-only or pre-registered authorization server cannot know. This is a false positive that blocks the run. Inferring the cause from the status code alone is a heuristic, and the project's severity principle caps heuristics at warning. Medium is the right severity: it needs --active-auth, but in that mode it reliably gives a false error for every server that uses CIMD only or pre-registered clients. A likely fix: count a 400 as a redirect rejection only when the body names redirect_uri. Otherwise downgrade it to a warning or info, or skip it when no DCR client_id was obtained. I removed the worktree afterwards.

findings.title: SRV-004 reports a public host as 'resolves only locally, not in public DNS' (error) when the DNS resolver itself fails
findings.claim: lookupHost sets d.error whenever both resolve4 and resolve6 reject, whatever the code. SRV-004 then builds `local` with `(d.lookup ?? []).filter((ip) => isIP(ip) === 4 || !!d.error)` before it looks at the error code. A resolver failure (ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEOUT, ESERVFAIL: blocked UDP/53, a sandbox, a flaky corporate resolver) combined with a working system lookup therefore becomes an error for Claude and ChatGPT that names a public IP as local. The INCONCLUSIVE branch at line 132 cannot be reached in that case. dns.resolve* also does not query 'public DNS': it asks the resolvers in resolv.conf.
findings.repro: Ran it. A node script fed fake deps into dist/probe/network.js lookupHost: resolve4 and resolve6 reject with code ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEOUT or ESERVFAIL, and lookup returns ['93.184.215.14']. It then ran SRV_004.check on {target:{kind:'http'},transport:{dns:d},localMode:false}. All three codes gave `[{"message":"mcp.example.com resolves only locally (93.184.215.14), not in public DNS"}]`, which takes the rule severity: error for claude and chatgpt.
findings.fix: Treat the 'resolves only locally' case as proven only when the resolver returned an authoritative 'no records' answer (d.code ENOTFOUND or ENODATA, or a fulfilled empty answer). For any other d.code (ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEOUT, ESERVFAIL, EREFUSED, ...) return the INCONCLUSIVE info and include the system-lookup addresses in the message. Also say 'configured resolver' instead of 'public DNS'. Patch release.

votes.evidence: Read at bc7090d with git show; no worktree created. In src/probe/network.ts:102-116, lookupHost runs resolve4, resolve6 and dns.lookup in parallel. It keeps the lookup addresses whenever lookup returns any, and it sets res.error and res.code whenever both resolve4 and resolve6 reject, whatever the code. In src/rules/server.ts:124, SRV-004 computes `local = d.a.length ? [] : (d.lookup ?? []).filter((ip) => isIP(ip) === 4 || !!d.error)` and pushes "resolves only locally ... not in public DNS" before it checks d.code. So with resolve* failing (ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEOUT, ESERVFAIL), d.a stays empty and a public IPv4 from lookup lands in `local`. That makes the ENOTFOUND/ENODATA/INCONCLUSIVE branch at lines 125-132 unreachable whenever lookup succeeded. The only guards are these: localize() downgrades the finding to info only when snap.localMode is set; connect.ts:419 sets localMode from isLocalTarget(dns) (util/net.ts:76), which uses every address including lookup, so a public IP like 93.184.215.14 keeps localMode false. The auth probe's asDns (auth.ts:151) takes the same path. Result: an error for claude and chatgpt (rule severity) that names a public IP as local, which is a false positive. It is a heuristic in an environment with a broken resolver, and the project's principle says such output should be at most an info or inconclusive finding. The wording "public DNS" is also inaccurate: dns.resolve* asks the resolvers in resolv.conf. I did not re-run the repro, but the code path matches it exactly. Medium fits because it needs a resolver failure (sandboxes, CI, blocked UDP/53), but the outcome is a hard false BLOCKED verdict.

Code at bc7090d: in src/probe/network.ts:102-116, lookupHost sets res.error/res.code whenever resolve4 and resolve6 both reject, whatever the code. It stores dns.lookup results in res.lookup on its own. In src/rules/server.ts:124 SRV-004 computes `local = d.a.length ? [] : (d.lookup ?? []).filter((ip) => isIP(ip) === 4 || !!d.error)`, pushes "resolves only locally ... not in public DNS" and does `continue` before the error-code branch, so the INCONCLUSIVE branch (line ~132) is never reached when lookup answered. The finding has no severity override, so the rule severity applies: error for claude and chatgpt. I built a detached worktree at bc7090d (npm ci, npm run build) and ran a node script with fake deps through dist/probe/network.js lookupHost and dist/rules/server.js SRV_004.check (http target, localMode false, lookup -> ['93.184.215.14']). ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEOUT and ESERVFAIL on both resolvers each gave [{"message":"mcp.example.com resolves only locally (93.184.215.14), not in public DNS"}]. A variant reaches the same false error without d.error: resolve4 ETIMEOUT while resolve6 succeeds, because the IPv4 filter still matches. The existing tests (test/rules/server.test.ts:222-245) cover ESERVFAIL only with no lookup result, and "local" only with ENOTFOUND or an empty A. A transient or resolver-level failure with a working system lookup is not covered. The real deps use dns.resolve4/resolve6 (c-ares, the resolv.conf servers, not "public DNS") and dns.lookup (getaddrinfo), so this split happens in practice: blocked UDP/53, sandboxes, flaky resolvers. Result: a deterministic-looking error on a public host from an environmental failure, which goes against the project rule that error is reserved for deterministic detection. Severity medium: it is a false blocking verdict, but it depends on the environment. Worktree removed.

findings.title: In an auth-required (or token-rejected) run, rules that need nothing count as passed: SRV-013, SPEC-002, SPEC-020, SRV-011, SRV-015 and others show as passed in JUnit
findings.claim: The A10-05 fix skips empty results only when `snap.fatal || toolLevel === 'connect-failed'`. When the server answers 401 and no --bearer is given, there is no initialize result, no lists and no probes. Even so, every rule with `needs: []` (SPEC-002/008/016/017/018/020/021/023 and SRV-011..015) finds nothing and is counted in rulesRun. JUnit lists them as passed testcases, for example `SPEC-020 List methods for declared capabilities succeed` and `SRV-011`, although tools/list never ran. The verdict says INCOMPLETE, but per-rule outputs (JUnit, SARIF rule list, rulesRun) claim checks that never happened. This is the usual CI case of a job without a token.
findings.repro: Ran it. The loopback OAuth stub answers 401 to every MCP request. `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:47812/mcp --format json`: coverage is auth-required, and SRV-011, SRV-012, SRV-013, SRV-014, SRV-015, SPEC-002, SPEC-008, SPEC-016, SPEC-017, SPEC-018, SPEC-020, SPEC-021 and SPEC-023 appear neither in findings nor in skipped, so they passed. The same run with `--format junit` contains `<testcase classname="claude" name="SPEC-020 List methods for declared capabilities succeed"/>` and `SRV-015`/`SRV-011` testcases with no <skipped/>.
findings.fix: Extend the line-236 condition to toolLevel 'auth-required' and 'token-rejected' when the rule is not URL_ONLY and not an auth rule (needs 'auth', 'active-auth' or 'http' alone with URL-only data). Use authReason(snap) as the skip reason. An alternative is to give these rules an explicit 'server' need that unmetNeed fails unless initializeRaw or discoverRaw is set. Add a test with an auth-required snapshot. Rules that were wrongly passing become skipped, so this is a patch release, as A10-05 was in 1.0.1.

votes.evidence:
Code: src/rules/engine.ts:236 skips a rule with empty results only when `snap.fatal || toolLevel === 'connect-failed'`. In the auth path, src/connect.ts:479 (`rejected()`) sets coverage to `auth-required` (or `token-rejected` when credentials were sent) and does NOT set snap.fatal. So rules with `needs: []` go through unmetNeed() without a reason, return [] and are counted in rulesRun. authReason() covers auth-required and token-rejected, but it is only used through the needs-based checks (list needs, ui and so on), so it gives no guard here. junit.ts:49 adds its synthetic error case only for fatal or stopped runs.

The 127.0.0.1 stub answers 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header to every request. `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:47813/mcp --format json` gave coverage `{toolLevel:'auth-required'}`. JSON run (`--format json`):
