improvements.title: Validate prompt, resource and resource-template list entries against the schema
improvements.detail: No rule checks the shape of prompts/list, resources/list or resources/templates/list items. Missing or non-string Prompt.name, PromptArgument.name, non-boolean PromptArgument.required, Resource.uri and Resource.name, non-string mimeType, and a malformed RFC 6570 uriTemplate all pass silently. I verified this with /tmp/claude-1000/-home-kali-packages/fae74d01-791a-469a-ab5f-90cdb063ebe5/scratchpad/raw-server.mjs: the report says 'Checked 2 tools · 1 resource · 2 prompts' and has no SPEC finding. These are schema-required fields and the check is deterministic, so it could be spec=error. A new SPEC-025 rule fits.

improvements.title: Claude plugin checklist: blocking checks LST does not cover yet
improvements.detail: The pre-submission checklist blocks several things the LST rules do not check. Blocks: displayName and author.name in mixed scripts or with invisible characters; component keys misspelled or placed under 'experimental'; plugin.json component paths that point outside the plugin folder; hooks/hooks.json that is invalid JSON, lacks a top-level hooks or modules object, uses an unknown event or type, or has a non-https HTTP hook; skill, command or agent front matter that does not parse or a description that is not a string; component folder or file names with the wrong capitalization (hooks/, skills/, SKILL.md). 'Validation stops': Windows-invalid names (colon, trailing dot or space, CON/PRN), case-only collisions, .gitattributes export-ignore/export-subst/filter, any file over 5 MiB. Held for a reviewer, which could be a warning: a lockfile next to package.json, an MCP server started through a shell, -c or npm run, and a credential read from an env var such as $GITHUB_TOKEN. All of this is deterministic file inspection.

improvements.title: ChatGPT package manifest: name, version, description, skills and translations limits
improvements.detail: Several package fields from the submission pages are not checked. name: 64 characters or fewer, starting with an ASCII letter or digit, then letters, digits, _ or -. version: an explicit semver of 64 characters or fewer. Plugin description: 1,024 characters or fewer (plugin_description_too_long); the submission page says 4000, so cite both. author.name 120, email 320, URL 2048 https; homepage https 2048. skills/get-started/SKILL.md must have name and description front matter, the skill description must be 1,024 characters or fewer, and plugin-name:skill-name 64 or fewer. Translations: a non-empty locale key, subtitle on one line of 30 characters or fewer, description 4000 or fewer, no tabs or control characters. A protected server must not be configured as type 'none' (cross-check with authProbe). LST-016 and LST-017 cover none of these today.

improvements.title: Heuristic for categories both directories exclude: adult content, gambling and other prohibited goods
improvements.detail: Claude policy 4.D excludes software that primarily serves 18+ content, and 4.A generally excludes crypto. OpenAI prohibits adult content, gambling, drugs, weapons, tobacco, malware and surveillance, and fake IDs. POL-001..005 do not cover these. In my repro, the tools place_bet ('Place a sports bet on a casino wager with real money') and adult_videos ('explicit 18+ adult porn videos') produced no POL finding. A new POL-006 at warning level (heuristic, per the severity principle) would help reviewers.

improvements.title: Implied OpenAI or Anthropic endorsement in serverInfo name/title
improvements.detail: POL-003 already has an ENDORSE pattern ('official chatgpt', 'endorsed by openai'), but it runs over the tool corpus only. A server named 'Official ChatGPT Betting' produced no finding in my repro. OpenAI says plugins 'must not imply OpenAI made or endorses them', and the Claude plugin checklist blocks names that present the plugin as official. Running ENDORSE, plus a brand check for OpenAI, ChatGPT, Anthropic and Claude, over serverInfo name, title and description would catch this. It partly overlaps with A11-01.

improvements.title: Validate MRTR inputRequests: elicitation requestedSchema and URL mode
improvements.detail: SPEC-021 reads inputRequests only to flag deprecated sampling and roots. An elicitation/create inputRequest seen in an input_required result or an --active call is not validated. The requestedSchema must be a flat object of primitive properties (string, number, integer, boolean, or enum). URL mode needs an https url, and the 2026-07-28 removal of elicitationId and notifications/elicitation/complete is not checked either.

improvements.title: Tool.execution.taskSupport value check
improvements.detail: Tool.execution.taskSupport (forbidden | optional | required) is not validated. A value of 'required' on a server Claude talks to also means Claude, which does not support tasks, cannot call the tool. That should be a SRV-015 info, with a spec error for an unknown value.

improvements.title: Claude mobile: camera, microphone and geolocation permissions unavailable
improvements.detail: The design guidelines say apps on Claude mobile have no camera, microphone or location access. APPS-017 already parses _meta.ui.permissions. A claude=info note when camera, microphone or geolocation is requested would tell authors to provide a fallback.

improvements.title: ChatGPT frame domains need a review explanation
improvements.detail: submission-errors has frame_domain_explanation_required, and plugin-guidelines require embedded pages to come from the server's own registrable domain. APPS-008 already computes third-party frames. Its ChatGPT message could name the explanation the dashboard asks for, and MAN items could list each external frame domain.

improvements.title: High-risk domains: human-in-the-loop and disclosure reminder
improvements.detail: Claude policy 1.B asks software in legal, healthcare, insurance or finance to provide human-in-the-loop measures and consumer disclosure. When tool text matches those domains, a conditional MAN item (or an info heuristic) would surface it. Today only POL-001 covers money transfer.

findings.title: INJ-001 and the other INJ/DATA/POL rules skip serverInfo title/description, resource and template name/title, and prompt name/title
findings.claim: buildCorpus feeds the content rules only tool fields, schema text, instructions, prompt and argument descriptions, and resource or template descriptions. Several fields are never scanned: serverInfo.title and serverInfo.description (the 2025-11-25 Implementation fields), serverInfo from server/discover, resource and resourceTemplate name and title, and prompt name and title. Clients show these strings to users and the model. The directory policy 2.G and the review criteria reject hidden, obfuscated or encoded instructions anywhere in the Software, and INJ-001 is an error-level rule for that requirement. A server can therefore hide a Unicode-tag-encoded instruction plus a bidi override in those fields and pass INJ-001 with no finding. Round 3's A05-01 widened the corpus to schema titles, enums and defaults only, so this is a different gap.
findings.repro: I ran this against the bc7090d build. The scratch server is /tmp/claude-1000/-home-kali-packages/fae74d01-791a-469a-ab5f-90cdb063ebe5/scratchpad/hidden-server.mjs, a raw JSON-RPC stdio server. It puts 'Notes' + U+E0000-tagged 'ignore previous instructions' + U+202E into serverInfo.title, serverInfo.description, a resource name and title, a resource template name and title, a prompt title, and a prompt name with a tag character. Command: node dist/cli.js --stdio "node .../hidden-server.mjs" --format json. Result: only SPEC-010 info, SRV-002 info x2, TOOL-027 info and TOOL-028 info. There was no INJ-001 finding.
findings.fix: In buildCorpus, push serverInfo.title, serverInfo.description and serverInfo.name, plus the discover serverInfo when present (where 'server.*'). Push resource name/title, resourceTemplate name/title and prompt name/title (where 'resource.name', 'prompt.title' and so on, with subject set). Add a corpus-where filter so that rules unsuited to names (INJ-008, TOOL-008 style) can opt out. INJ-001, INJ-002 and INJ-003 should see all of these fields. Add a fixture test using the payload above. This is a patch release: detection widens under an existing rule ID.

votes.evidence: Code read at bc7090d: buildCorpus in src/rules/util/text.ts:226-263 only adds tool name/title/annotations.title/description, schema text (description, title, enum/const, default/examples, property keys), instructions, prompt.description, prompt argument descriptions, resource.description and resourceTemplate.description. It never adds serverInfo.title or serverInfo.description (connect.ts:224/233 fills snap.serverInfo from both initialize and server/discover _meta), resource or template name/title, or prompt name/title. INJ-001 (injection.ts:117-134, error for claude and chatgpt) runs hiddenChars only over corpus(snap,{samples,keys}). No other rule calls hiddenChars (git grep finds only injection.ts:92/127). The other serverInfo consumers (POL at policy.ts:159, SRV naming at server.ts:327-344, SRV-013, SPEC-017 icons) check product words, suffixes, name/version shape or icons, not hidden characters. So nothing else guards these fields. docs/design/spec.md §1.5 (line 80) lists the same corpus 'where' set, so the gap is in the spec as well as the code. It is not a deviation from the spec, and it is not covered by round-3 A05-01, which widened the corpus to schema fields only. Repro: I ran the existing bc7090d build in the review-r4/scratch/find-A09 worktree, as a read-only run, against the finding's hidden-server.mjs. The report's serverInfo.title and description contain U+E0000-tagged 'ignore previous instructions' plus U+202E. The only findings were SPEC-010 info, SRV-002 info x2, TOOL-027 info and TOOL-028 info, with no INJ-001. Severity: medium is right. Tag and bidi detection is deterministic and INJ-001 is already error-level for this policy requirement, but the gap is limited to fields that are shown less prominently than tool descriptions. I created no worktree of my own, so there was nothing to remove.

Built bc7090d in a detached worktree (removed afterwards). In src/rules/util/text.ts, buildCorpus pushes tool name/title/annotations.title/description, schema text, instructions, prompt.description, prompt argument descriptions, resource.description and resourceTemplate.description. It never reads snap.serverInfo (title/description), resource or template name/title, or prompt name/title. The only uses of serverInfo in the rules are in server.ts (SRV suffix and name checks, SRV-013), and none of them do a hidden-character scan. Running node dist/cli.js --stdio "node <scratchpad>/hidden-server.mjs" --format json put a Unicode-tag-encoded 'ignore previous instructions' plus U+202E in serverInfo.title/description, a resource name/title, a template name/title, a prompt title and a tagged prompt name. The output had only SPEC-010, SRV-002 x2, TOOL-027 and TOOL-028 (all info). There was no INJ, DATA or POL finding. Control: the same string placed only in a resource description produced INJ-001 error 'resource.description: tag or bidi control characters ...'. The detector works, so the miss is caused only by the corpus scope. This is a deterministic false negative for an error-level rule on strings that clients show. It differs from round 3 A05-01, which covered schema titles, enums and defaults. Medium severity fits: the check can be bypassed, but only through the less prominent metadata fields.

findings.title: SRV-003 rates an SSE-only server as a warning for ChatGPT, but OpenAI lists Streamable HTTP as a production-endpoint requirement
findings.claim: https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/mcp-server, under 'Deploy the endpoint', lists the production endpoint requirements and includes 'Support the MCP streamable HTTP transport.' The page never mentions SSE. Detection is deterministic: SRV-003 fires only when the Streamable HTTP POST was rejected and HTTP+SSE worked. Under the project rule (error for a documented MUST with deterministic detection) the chatgpt severity should be error. The rule's sources cite only the Claude policy, which says 'should support' (warning is right for Claude), and the spec page, not the OpenAI page. A ChatGPT verdict for an SSE-only server therefore reads WARN instead of BLOCKED.
findings.repro: Not run: the fixtures in this area have no SSE-only HTTP server. Read from the code: server.ts:106 returns { message: 'legacy HTTP+SSE only; Streamable HTTP POST was rejected' } with the default severity map { claude: 'warning', chatgpt: 'warning', spec: 'warning' }.
findings.fix: Set severity to { claude: 'warning', chatgpt: 'error', spec: 'warning' } and add https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/mcp-server to sources. Add a severityNote saying Claude 'should support' while OpenAI requires it for production. Raising a severity changes exit codes, so ship it in a minor release and note it in CHANGELOG under the stability policy.

votes.evidence: At bc7090d, src/rules/server.ts:84 gives SRV-003 the severity map { claude: 'warning', chatgpt: 'warning', spec: 'warning' }. Line 88 lists only two sources, the Claude directory policy and the spec STREAMABLE_HTTP page; OAI_MCP is defined at line 16 but SRV-003 does not cite it. Line 106 returns a finding without a severity override when snap.transport.kind === 'sse'. Detection is deterministic. connect.ts tries SSE only after the Streamable HTTP POST initialize returned HTTP 400, 404 or 405 with no modern error body. connect.ts:349-350 sets kind 'sse' only when the SSE handshake completes, and connect.ts:450 sets it when the SSE GET answered 200 or 401. No other rule in src/ raises a ChatGPT error for an SSE-only server: a grep for 'sse' in the rules finds only skips and timing code. WebFetch of https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/mcp-server, section 'Deploy the endpoint', which is scoped 'For public plugin submission', reads: 'The production endpoint must: - Support the MCP streamable HTTP transport.' The page never mentions SSE. This is a documented MUST with deterministic detection, so the project's severity principle calls for chatgpt=error, and OAI_MCP should be added to sources. The issue is not in the round-1 or round-3 FINDINGS or in REMEDIATION. Round 3's A10-07 was about the connect-failure path, not SSE severity. Not run: no fixture is an SSE-only HTTP server.

areas.name: usability for CI integrators and power users (cross-cutting)
areas.coverage: Read at bc7090d in a detached worktree (npm ci --ignore-scripts and npm run build OK; the worktree is removed): action.yml in full, src/config.ts in full, src/cli.ts in full, src/baseline.ts in full, src/report/sarif.ts, junit.ts, github.ts and index.ts in full, the drift.ts exports, docs/guide/ci.md and options-and-config.md in full, the README Stability policy, CHANGELOG 1.1.0, and grep of round-3 FINDINGS/REMEDIATION for drift/config items (none of the above re-reports them). Ran against the built CLI with test/fixtures/good-server.mjs, bad-server.mjs and listing/*: the baseline save and synthetic drift in 4 formats under GITHUB_ACTIONS (A12-01), the Action-equivalent command line with a discovered config (A12-02), the SARIF automationDetails ids (A12-03), the documented first-baseline recipe in a fresh dir (A12-04), the SARIF level vs gated annotation counts with --target claude (A12-05), a listing-only run (A12-06), the config sarifLocation warning (A12-08), duplicate --format (A12-09), and $schema in the config. Not run: the real GitHub Action and the code-scanning/upload-sarif behaviour (A12-03 and A12-05 rely on GitHub's documented category and threshold semantics), a GitLab pipeline (A12-07 is reasoned from the recipe plus the verified drift exit code), Windows and macOS runners (the action's bash was only read: the bash 3.2 empty-array guard and the IFS split look right), upgrading with a 1.0.x baseline (no older report at hand), the vitest suites, and the markdown/text renderers beyond the Result line. No network access other than local fixtures.

improvements.title: Per-finding suppression with a justification (and SARIF suppressions)
improvements.detail: --ignore is rule-wide only and has no reason. Add a config key such as "suppress": [{"rule": "TOOL-013", "tool": "search", "path": "/properties/q", "reason": "...", "expires": "2027-01-01"}]. Matching should use the baseline subject key (rule, tool or resource, path). Suppressed findings go to JSON `ignored` with the reason, and to SARIF as results with suppressions[{kind:'external', justification}] (today ignored findings are missing from SARIF, so code-scanning alerts close as 'fixed'). JUnit and text should show the reason. Warn when a suppression or an --ignore matched nothing (stale), and fail when one has expired.

improvements.title: Several servers in one config / one run (monorepo)
improvements.detail: A config file can name a single server only. Add "servers": {"a": {"stdio": ..., "cwd": ...}, "b": {"url": ...}} with per-server overrides and per-server baseline paths, plus --server <name> to pick one. Output would be one SARIF run per server, each with its own automationDetails category (fixes A12-03 by construction), one JUnit testsuite per server and platform, and an aggregated exit code. The Action would then need only one step.

improvements.title: `mcp-review-check init`
improvements.detail: Write a commented starter mcp-review-check.config.json (server detected from package.json bin/main or .mcp.json), mkdir .mcp-review-check, write the first baseline with --fail-on never, and print the matching GitHub Action / GitLab snippet. This removes the first-run friction found in A12-04 and the guesswork about which keys exist.

improvements.title: JSON Schema for the config file, and accept a "$schema" key
improvements.detail: "$schema" in the config is a usage error today ('unknown key "$schema"'), so editors cannot offer completion or validation. Ship schema/config.schema.json, generated from KEYS in src/config.ts, in the package. Accept and ignore "$schema" (and perhaps keys starting with "//" for comments). Verified: --config with {"$schema":"x","failOn":"warning"} gives exit 2.

improvements.title: Rule catalog: addedIn / changedIn and deterministic-vs-heuristic in --list-rules --format json
improvements.detail: Before upgrading a minor, an integrator wants 'what can newly fail my gate'. Add addedIn and severityRaisedIn (version) and kind: deterministic|heuristic to each rule in the JSON catalog and to SARIF rule properties. Add --list-rules --since 1.0 to print only the rules added or raised since that version. This fits the stability policy's 'read CHANGELOG before upgrading a minor'.

improvements.title: SARIF rule metadata for GitHub: help.markdown, tags, security-severity
improvements.detail: Rules carry only help.text. Add help.markdown (the fix with code formatting and the source links), tags ['security'] for the INJ/AUTH/DATA rules with properties['security-severity'], so they show as security alerts with a severity, plus defaultConfiguration.level. Code scanning renders these in the alert view.

improvements.title: Action inputs: working-directory, sarif-location/category, baseline, fail-on-incomplete, fail-on-drift; outputs: tool-changes
improvements.detail: Common CI needs go through untyped extra-args today. Add first-class inputs: working-directory (passed as --cwd and used for config discovery), sarif-location plus upload category (A12-03), baseline, fail-on-incomplete and fail-on-drift. Add a `tool-changes` output so a later step can tell a drift failure from a finding failure (both are exit 1).

improvements.title: Cache the npm install in the Action
improvements.detail: Each Action run does `npm install mcp-review-check@<range>` into RUNNER_TEMP with no cache. Use actions/cache keyed on the resolved version (from npm view), or document `cli-path` with a cached global install. Every job saves a few seconds plus one registry round-trip.

improvements.title: JUnit suite naming for several servers
improvements.detail: Testsuites are named only by platform ('claude') with classname 'claude'. Two JUnit files from two servers in one GitLab pipeline or dorny report get identical suite and case names. Add the server name (serverInfo.name or --sarif-location) to the suite name and classname (e.g. 'claude · acme-notes'), or add a --report-name option.

improvements.title: Check that output directories exist before connecting
improvements.detail: Besides creating parent directories (A12-04), validate that --output, --json-output and --save-baseline are writable during argument validation. A typo then costs a usage error instead of a full run (which, with --active, includes tool calls) followed by exit 2.

findings.title: A --fail-on-drift failure exits 1 while every artifact says PASS: Result line, summary.failed, JUnit, annotations and the Action's verdict output
findings.claim: When --fail-on-drift fails the run (a changed tool or 'not compared'), the exit code is 1, but resultLine() still prints 'Result: PASS (--fail-on error)', JSON summary.failed is false, the JUnit report has failures="0" (drift goes only to <system-out>), no ::error annotation is printed, and the Action's `verdict` output (computed from summary.failed) is PASS next to exit-code=1. A GitLab test view and the GitHub job show a red job with an all-green report and nothing that names the cause. The 'verdicts and summary.failed stay about findings' sentence in options-and-config.md documents the JSON part, but the Result line, JUnit, the annotations and the Action verdict have no drift signal at all. This is the same gap A10-01 closed for --fail-on-incomplete.
findings.repro: Ran: node dist/cli.js --no-config --fail-on never --save-baseline .r/base.json --stdio -- node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs; changed toolFingerprints[0].sha256 and fields.description in a copy (.r/drift.json); then for f in text json junit sarif: GITHUB_ACTIONS=true GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=.r/sum.md node dist/cli.js --no-config --baseline .r/drift.json --fail-on-drift --format $f --output .r/out.$f --stdio -- node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs. Every run gave exit=1, 0 lines starting with '::', the stderr summary '... 1 tool change (--fail-on-drift) · PASS (--fail-on error)', JSON summary.failed=false with gate.reason=null, JUnit failures="0", and the text report 'Result: PASS (--fail-on error)'.
findings.fix: Handle a drift failure like A10-01: when failOnDrift && (changes>0 || notCompared), have the head of resultLine read 'FAIL (--fail-on-drift)' (or add '· N tool changes (--fail-on-drift)' to a FAIL head); in JUnit add one '<testcase name="tool-definition drift">' with a <failure type="drift"> per suite; in annotations() add one ::error titled mcp-review-check naming the changed tools, or the not-compared reason; add a JSON field (e.g. summary.driftFailed or baseline.failed, which is additive and fine for a minor) and have the Action derive verdict FAIL from it and expose a `tool-changes` output. Keep summary.failed about findings if that contract matters, but no human-facing line should say PASS on exit 1.

votes.evidence:
I read the code at bc7090d with `git show` and did not run it. The code path is deterministic.

- **Exit code:** src/cli.ts:835 is `code = ... : report.summary.failed || textOpts.failOnDrift || notCompared ? 1 : 0`. Drift is added to the exit code only here. `buildReport` (src/report/index.ts:47-71) never hears about drift, so `summary.failed` and `gate.reason` stay about findings and `incompleteFails`.
- **Result line:** `resultLine()` (index.ts:188-212) uses only `s.failed`. It prints `PASS (--fail-on X)`. The text report (text.ts:176), the markdown report (markdown.ts:60) and the stderr summary line (cli.ts:839) all use it.
- **JUnit:** `renderJunit` (junit.ts:91-110) puts drift only in `<system-out>`, and the doc comment says "never a failure either". The failure counts come only from findings, so the report has `failures="0"`.
- **Annotations:** `annotations()` in github.ts reads only fatal, stopped, `toolLevel`/`incompleteFails` and findings, so drift gets no `::error`.
- **Action:** action.yml computes `verdict` from `r.summary.failed`, so it outputs PASS next to `exit-code=1`.
- **Contrast with A10-01:** for --fail-on-incomplete, `buildReport` sets `failed`, `gate.reason`, a JUnit `<error>` and an `::error` annotation. --fail-on-drift got none of these.
- **Docs:** docs/guide/options-and-config.md:23 says only "The verdicts and `summary.failed` stay about findings". The PASS Result line, JUnit with no failure and no annotation are not documented.

**Overstated part:** the claim that nothing names the cause goes too far.
- For a real tool change, `textOpts.failOnDrift` is true. Then the drift heading in the text report and the markdown report/GitHub job summary reads "Changed tool definitions (N since baseline) · fails the run (--fail-on-drift)" (drift.ts:186-188). The stderr summary also says "N tool change (--fail-on-drift)".
- For the "not compared" case, stderr prints the `--fail-on-drift: tool definitions not compared ...` warning (cli.ts:834). The headings do not carry the note there, because `changes` is 0.

The rest holds as stated: the Result line reads PASS, JSON `failed` is false, JUnit has `failures="0"`, there is no annotation and the Action verdict is PASS while the exit code is 1.

**Severity:** medium is right. This is a CI/UX inconsistency, not a correctness or security bug. The exit code is correct.

I built bc7090d in a detached worktree, which I have since removed. I saved a baseline from good-server.mjs, then set toolFingerprints[0].sha256 and fields.description to other valid hex digests. I ran with GITHUB_ACTIONS=true and --baseline drift.json --fail-on-drift once for each of --format text, json, junit and sarif.

What every run showed:
- Exit code 1, with 0 lines starting with '::' on stdout and stderr, so no ::error or ::warning annotation.
- The stderr line reads '... 1 tool change (--fail-on-drift) · PASS (--fail-on error)'.
- The text report says 'Result: PASS (--fail-on error)'.
- In the JSON, summary.failed=false and gate.reason=null.
- The JUnit has failures="0" in both suites. The drift ('Changed tool definitions ... ~ search_notes: changed: description') appears only in <system-out>.
- The step-summary table row says 'Result | PASS'.

In action.yml (around line 195) the verdict is set to `limits.stopped ? INCOMPLETE : summary.failed ? FAIL : PASS`, so the Action would output verdict=PASS next to exit-code=1.

For comparison, --fail-on-incomplete got this treatment in A10-01: src/report/junit.ts:53-57 adds an <error type="incomplete">, and src/report/github.ts:41-44 prints an ::error. Drift has neither; junit.ts:107 says drift is 'never a failure'.

docs/design/spec.md:1317 states on purpose that drift does not change the verdicts or summary.failed. Under --fail-on-drift, only the section heading and the --output summary line mention the failure. So the JSON part is documented behaviour.

The claim that 'nothing names the cause' goes too far. The text report's drift section, the stderr line and the step-summary heading all say 'fails the run (--fail-on-drift)'. Still, the PASS Result line, JUnit failures=0, the missing annotation and Action verdict=PASS next to exit 1 all reproduce. It is the same inconsistency A10-01 fixed for --fail-on-incomplete, so medium (ux) is the right severity.

findings.title: The Action always passes --target and --fail-on, silently overriding the project's config file
findings.claim: The `platform` and `fail-on` inputs default to 'all' and 'error', and the run step always puts `--target "$platform" --fail-on "$INPUT_FAIL_ON"` on the command line. Command-line options win over the config file, so a repository's mcp-review-check.config.json with "target": "claude" and "failOn": "warning" is ignored under the Action without any note. The same file does apply locally and in the npx recipes, so the Action gates differently from a developer's run. fail-on-spec and active, which are passed only when true, do follow the file, so the inputs are inconsistent with one another.
findings.repro: Ran in a directory holding mcp-review-check.config.json = {"failOn":"warning","target":"claude","failOnSpec":true} the Action's command line: node dist/cli.js --target all --fail-on error --format sarif --output x.sarif --json-output j.json --stdio "node test/fixtures/bad-server.mjs". The JSON gate.platforms is ['claude','chatgpt','spec'] and the Result line is 'FAIL (--fail-on error, --fail-on-spec)', so the file's target and failOn were dropped and its failOnSpec was kept.
findings.fix: Default `platform` and `fail-on` to '' and append --target/--fail-on only when the input is non-empty (the CLI defaults then apply, or the config file's values). Document in ci.md that an input overrides the config key. This changes the behaviour only for users who have a config file, which is the intended effect; state it in the CHANGELOG as a minor change.

votes.evidence: Read at bc7090d. action.yml: input `platform` defaults to `all` and `fail-on` to `error`. The run step always builds `args=(--target "$platform" --fail-on "$INPUT_FAIL_ON" --format sarif ...)`, while `--fail-on-spec` and `--active` are added only when the input is `true`. The CLI discovers the config file through findConfig(cwd) in src/cli.ts:522 when `--config` and `--no-config` are absent, and its help text (src/cli.ts:108) and CHANGELOG:268 say "Command-line options override the file". So under the Action a discovered mcp-review-check.config.json with `"target": "claude"` / `"failOn": "warning"` is always overridden by `--target all --fail-on error`, and no note is printed: the 'not used' notes in cli.ts:538-543 cover only other-transport and opposite keys, not a plain option replaced by a flag. A file `failOnSpec: true` still applies because the Action only ever adds `--fail-on-spec` and never `--no-fail-on-spec`. That matches the reported repro output (platforms claude/chatgpt/spec; 'FAIL (--fail-on error, --fail-on-spec)'). I found no guard and no documentation of this: neither action.yml nor docs/guide/ci.md mentions the config file being overridden, and round-3 FINDINGS has no related item. Effect: CI can gate less strictly than a local run (warning becomes error), with no message. A workaround exists: set the inputs to match the file. That justifies medium UX severity, not higher. Fix: default `platform` and `fail-on` to '' and pass them only when non-empty. This verdict comes from reading the code; I did not rebuild or rerun the repro.

Read action.yml at bc7090d: the `platform` input defaults to `all` and `fail-on` defaults to `error` (lines 22-29). The run step always builds `args=(--target "$platform" --fail-on "$INPUT_FAIL_ON" --format sarif ...)`. `--fail-on-spec` and `--active` are added only when their inputs are `true`. CHANGELOG and options docs say config-file options are "overridden by the command line". docs/guide/ci.md (the Action input table, lines 130-132) has no note that the Action overrides the file's `target` or `failOn`.

Repro: I built bc7090d in a detached worktree and ran it in a directory whose mcp-review-check.config.json held {"failOn":"warning","target":"claude","failOnSpec":true}.
(1) With the Action's command line (`--target all --fail-on error --format sarif --output x.sarif --json-output j.json --stdio "node test/fixtures/bad-server.mjs"`): stderr shows only "options from config file <path>" with no override note. JSON `target` is "all" and `summary.gate.platforms` is ["claude","chatgpt","spec"]. The Result line is "FAIL (--fail-on error, --fail-on-spec)". So the file's target and failOn were dropped and its failOnSpec was kept.
(2) Without those flags (a local or npx-style run): `target` is "claude", gate.platforms is ["claude","spec"], and the Result line is "FAIL (--fail-on warning, --fail-on-spec)". The gate counts the warnings.

So the Action gates differently from a local run, gives no notice, and treats its inputs inconsistently. A server with only warnings would pass under the Action but fail locally. That weakens a CI gate in silence. The workaround is easy (set the inputs to match the file). Medium fits.

Worktree removed.

findings.title: Several servers in one repository share a code-scanning category, so each SARIF upload replaces the other's alerts
findings.claim: The SARIF category is derived from --sarif-location only (automationDetails.id 'mcp-review-check/<location>/<startedAt>'). With the default location, every server checked in a repository uploads under category 'mcp-review-check/.mcp-review-check/'. In a monorepo with two Action steps (or a matrix), code scanning treats the second upload as a new analysis of the same category: the first server's alerts are shown as fixed and reappear on the next run. The Action has no `sarif-location` or `category` input, and ci.md does not tell a multi-server user to vary --sarif-location through extra-args.
findings.repro: Ran twice: node dist/cli.js --no-config --format sarif --stdio "node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs" | jq .runs[0].automationDetails.id gave 'mcp-review-check/.mcp-review-check/2026-11-05T02:24:05.034Z' and '.../2026-11-05T02:24:06.335Z'. Only the run part after the last '/' differs, so a run for a second server gets the same category. GitHub's upload behaviour per category: https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/integrating-with-code-scanning/sarif-support-for-code-scanning#runautomationdetails-object
findings.fix: Add a `sarif-location` input (passed as --sarif-location) and/or a `category` input forwarded to upload-sarif's `category`. Add a 'Several servers in one repository' recipe to ci.md (a matrix with sarif-location: servers/a, servers/b). Optionally default the location for a stdio target to something derived from the command or --cwd, in a minor release.

votes.evidence: Read at bc7090d without building, since the code paths settle the claim. In src/report/sarif.ts:76 the run gets `automationDetails: { id: \`mcp-review-check/${uri}/${r.startedAt}\` }`, where uri = artifactUri(location) and location defaults to SARIF_LOCATION '.mcp-review-check' (sarif.ts:12,27). The comment on line 75 says this is meant: "One code-scanning category (the id up to its last "/") per --sarif-location; the target is a run property." Nothing about the server (URL or stdio command) goes into the category. The target is only in runs[0].properties.target. partialFingerprints (sarif.ts:20) also leave out the target, so the two servers' alerts cannot be told apart either. In src/cli.ts:604, sarifLocation = values['sarif-location'] ?? SARIF_LOCATION. The config.ts sarifLocation key is the only other way to set it. Nothing derives it from the target. action.yml has no sarif-location or category input and always calls the CLI with `--format sarif --output $INPUT_SARIF_FILE` and no --sarif-location. The upload step passes only `sarif_file` to github/codeql-action/upload-sarif, with no `category`. docs/review/2026-11-01/remediation/W4D-report.md says this was a deliberate choice: "no `category` (the SARIF already carries `automationDetails.id`)". The SARIF already has automationDetails.id, so upload-sarif does not add its own matrix or job category. Two Action steps or matrix legs in one repo therefore upload under the same category, 'mcp-review-check/.mcp-review-check/', and per GitHub's runAutomationDetails docs the later upload replaces the earlier one's alerts for that category. In docs/guide/ci.md (lines 92-152 and the inputs table) and docs/guide/options-and-config.md:16, nothing tells a multi-server user to set a different `--sarif-location` per server through extra-args. That workaround works (extra-args is appended to the args), but it is not documented. FINDINGS.md for round 1 and round 3 do not cover this: F004 and A01/A10 are only about the warning when the flag is used with another format. Severity medium: no crash, but in a monorepo the code-scanning alerts are silently wrong (one server's alerts show as fixed, then reappear on the next run), and the only fix is an undocumented workaround.

I built the CLI at bc7090d in a detached worktree, which I removed afterwards. I ran it on two different servers, good-server.mjs and bad-server.mjs, with --format sarif. Both runs gave the same category in runs[0].automationDetails.id, 'mcp-review-check/.mcp-review-check/', and the same tool.driver.name, 'mcp-review-check'. Only the timestamp after the last '/' differed. The two targets differ only in properties.target, which code scanning does not use for the category.

Source: src/report/sarif.ts sets automationDetails.id to `mcp-review-check/${uri}/${r.startedAt}`. uri comes only from --sarif-location (default SARIF_LOCATION '.mcp-review-check'), and the code comment itself says 'One code-scanning category ... per --sarif-location'.

action.yml has no category or sarif-location input. The upload-sarif step passes only sarif_file, not `category`. Because the SARIF already carries an id, upload-sarif keeps it and does not derive a default category from the workflow, job and matrix. So even matrix jobs, which code scanning would otherwise keep apart, collide.

Docs: docs/guide/ci.md never mentions several servers, a matrix, a category or --sarif-location. options-and-config.md describes --sarif-location only as the artifact path, not as the category key.

Workaround works: extra-args '--sarif-location srv/b' gave the id 'mcp-review-check/srv/b/...', a separate category. The user just cannot find it in the docs.

This is not in the round 1 or round 3 FINDINGS. Round 1 F004 and round 3 A01/A10 are about --sarif-location warnings, which is a different issue.

Severity medium: alerts silently disappear and come back in multi-server repos. It is a UX and docs gap with a workaround, not a lint-correctness bug.

findings.title: The documented first-baseline command exits 2 in a fresh repository: the parent directory of --save-baseline is not created
findings.claim: ci.md:50 and walkthrough.md:62 tell the user to run `--save-baseline .mcp-review-check/baseline.json` as the first step. In a repository without a .mcp-review-check directory, writeFileSync fails with ENOENT after the whole check has run, and the run exits 2. Only the GitLab recipe has `mkdir -p`. The same applies to --output and --json-output, and so to the Action's `sarif-file: reports/x.sarif`.
findings.repro: Ran in an empty directory: node dist/cli.js --no-config --target claude --fail-on never --save-baseline .mcp-review-check/baseline.json --stdio -- node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs, which gave exit=2 and "error: cannot write --save-baseline .mcp-review-check/baseline.json: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.mcp-review-check/baseline.json'".
findings.fix: Create the parent directory (mkdirSync(dirname(path), {recursive:true})) before writing --save-baseline, --json-output and --output, as most report writers do. Otherwise check that the parent exists during validation, so the error comes as a usage error before connecting, and add `mkdir -p .mcp-review-check` to the two docs recipes (docs proposal).

votes.evidence: Read from bc7090d with git show. The finding's line numbers are off: the code is at src/cli.ts:857-873, not 781-793. The behaviour is as claimed. The only fs imports are lstatSync, readlinkSync, realpathSync, statSync and writeFileSync; src/cli.ts has no mkdirSync and no recursive directory creation. In the jsonOutputs loop (--json-output and --save-baseline), writeFileSync(path, jsonDoc) sits in a try/catch. A failure adds "error: cannot write <flag> <path>: ENOENT..." to writeErrors, and then finalCode = writeErrors ? 2 : code, so the run exits 2 after the full check. --output does the same at about line 870: writeFileSync(values.output, body) returns code 2, though it still prints the report to stdout. Nothing creates the directory first. The only guards are the unsaved check (fatal or stopped run) and the size warning. Docs: docs/guide/ci.md:50 and docs/guide/walkthrough.md:62 both give `--save-baseline .mcp-review-check/baseline.json` as the first run with no mkdir. Only the GitLab recipe (ci.md:226, 232) and the Docker recipe (ci.md:262) run `mkdir -p`. action.yml passes `--output "$INPUT_SARIF_FILE"` straight through and only creates the npm prefix dir (line 148). So a sarif-file input in a missing subdirectory (the default mcp-review-check.sarif is fine) leads to exit 2 and an empty sarif-file output. I did not re-run the repro; Node's writeFileSync raises ENOENT on a missing parent directory, which is what the reported message shows. Severity medium, not higher: the error message is clear and no data is lost, because stdout still has the report and the JSON goes to any writable path. But the documented quick-start step fails for every new repository.

Built bc7090d in a detached worktree and ran it from an empty directory. `node dist/cli.js --no-config --target claude --fail-on never --save-baseline .mcp-review-check/baseline.json --stdio -- node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs` exited 2 with "error: cannot write --save-baseline .mcp-review-check/baseline.json: ENOENT: no such file or directory". The full check ran before this failure. `--format sarif --output reports/x.sarif` exited 2 the same way with "cannot write --output reports/x.sarif: ENOENT". In src/cli.ts, the only fs imports are lstatSync, readlinkSync, realpathSync, statSync and writeFileSync, with no mkdirSync. The two writeFileSync calls are at lines 860 and 870 (the finding's line numbers are slightly off). The documented first-baseline command appears with no mkdir in docs/guide/ci.md:50 and docs/guide/walkthrough.md:62. Only the GitLab recipe (ci.md:226,232) and ci.md:262 run `mkdir -p`. action.yml passes `--output "$INPUT_SARIF_FILE"` with no mkdir, so a nested sarif-file path makes the step exit 2. On that failure the action sets the sarif-file output to empty, so the upload is skipped. It is a usability bug in documented paths and fails loudly, not silently, so medium is the right severity. Worktree removed.

findings.title: SARIF levels ignore the gate: ungated spec findings become code-scanning 'error' alerts while the annotations and exit code pass them
findings.claim: Annotations and the exit code use each finding's severity on the gated platforms (--target, plus spec only with --fail-on-spec). SARIF uses the finding's top severity whatever was gated. With --target claude and no --fail-on-spec, spec-only errors (APPS-001, SRV-018, TOOL-016 on bad-server) are uploaded as level 'error'. GitHub's code-scanning check fails a PR on error-level alerts by default (the 'Check runs failure threshold' setting), so the PR goes red on findings that the Action's own gate intentionally let pass.
findings.repro: Ran: GITHUB_ACTIONS=true node dist/cli.js --no-config --target claude --format sarif --stdio "node test/fixtures/bad-server.mjs". The output has 8 ::error annotations, but the SARIF has 11 results at level error. The 3 extra are spec-only (platforms: ['spec']), and 3 more spec-only results are at level warning.
findings.fix: Map each result's level from its severity on the gated platforms (as annotations() does), and use 'note' for findings that no gated platform counts. Keep the original severity in properties (severityByPlatform already has it, plus a properties.gated flag). As a less invasive alternative, add a --sarif-level gated|max switch with the default changing in a minor release. Docs: say in the SARIF row which severity code scanning sees. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/managing-your-code-scanning-configuration/editing-your-configuration-of-default-setup

votes.evidence: The behaviour is real: sarif.ts sets `level: LEVEL[f.severity]` from the top severity, while github.ts annotations follow the gated platforms. But it is a known item that the task says not to re-report. It is round 1 F122 (docs/review/2026-11-01/FINDINGS.md:94 and :2107, 'SARIF level берётся из максимальной severity по всем платформам, а не по gated'). It was raised again in round 3 under Improvements (docs/review/2026-11-04/FINDINGS.md:154, 'critic | ux | small | SARIF levels ignore the gate ... APPS-001, SRV-018, TOOL-016 on bad-server'), with the same example. The code has not regressed: it is unchanged, not newly broken.

findings.line: 135; also docs/guide/options-and-config.md --plugin-dir/--openai-manifest rows, --fail-on-drift row, Local mode paragraph
findings.title: Docs contradict the CLI and action.yml in four places

(2) options-and-config.md says --plugin-dir and --openai-manifest 'need a <url> or --stdio target', but --help and the code allow them alone as a listing-only run. (3) The --fail-on-drift row quotes the stderr message as always ending 're-save the baseline with --save-baseline', but since A01-07 the CLI says 'fix this run (see the coverage line) before saving a baseline from it' when the run is the side that failed. For (1), compare action.yml:46 `default: '1.1'` with ci.md:135. For (3) and (4), read src/cli.ts (advice for notComparedBy==='run'; banner condition includes junit).
findings.fix: Docs proposals (another session owns docs): set the table default to `1.1` and generate the input table from action.yml in CI to prevent drift; reword the two rows to 'with a <url> or --stdio target it is added to the check; alone it runs listing-only'; quote both advice variants; say 'json, sarif and junit'.

(2) options-and-config.md:35-36 says --plugin-dir/--openai-manifest 'needs a <url> or --stdio target'. But cli.ts:593-594 allows a listing-only run, and --help (cli.ts:88,92) says 'Alone ... a listing-only run'. `node dist/cli.js --no-config --plugin-dir test/fixtures/listing/openai-invalid --quiet` ran the LST checks without connecting. It exited 1, not 0 as the repro says, because that folder fails LST-001/004/005; the contradiction still holds. findings.title: GitLab recipe: an intended tool change makes the default branch fail on drift forever, and the cached baseline can never be refreshed
findings.claim: The recipe passes --fail-on-drift on the default branch too, and refreshes the cached baseline only from a successful default-branch job. After an intended tool change is merged, every default-branch job exits 1 on drift, so after_script never copies the new report, and the cached baseline (which the notes say not to commit) keeps the old fingerprints. The only way out is to clear the runner cache by hand or edit the CI file, and the guide mentions neither.
findings.repro: Followed the recipe's logic: on the default branch, `--baseline ... --fail-on-drift` gives exit 1 on any tool change (verified in A12-01: exit=1 with a changed fingerprint). after_script requires CI_JOB_STATUS=success, so the cache is never updated.
findings.fix: Docs proposal: pass --fail-on-drift only for merge_request_event pipelines (the default branch records the accepted state), or document 'CI/CD > Pipelines > Clear runner caches' as the way to accept a change. A cleaner fix is a dedicated refresh job (when: manual) that runs with --save-baseline.

votes.evidence: In the ci.md GitLab recipe, the default-branch job also runs `--baseline .mcp-review-check/baseline.json --fail-on-drift` when a cached baseline exists. after_script copies the new report into the cache only if `$CI_JOB_STATUS = success` on the default branch. After an intended tool change is merged, each default-branch run exits 1 on drift, so the cached baseline is never replaced. GitLab's default cache `when: on_success` also skips the cache upload on a failed job. Every later default-branch pipeline therefore fails until someone clears the runner cache by hand or edits the CI file. The same lock-in happens when a new finding is accepted on the default branch. The Notes mention committing the baseline instead, and a missing cache, but give no way out of this state.

findings.title: A config file's sarifLocation warns on every non-SARIF run, unlike quiet/checklist/diffOnly
findings.claim: formatWarnings deliberately warns only for switches given on the command line ('one file serves runs in several formats'). The --sarif-location warning instead tests the merged values, so a shared config file with sarifLocation (needed for the monorepo case in A12-03) prints 'warning: --sarif-location applies only to --format sarif' on every text, JSON or markdown run, and names a flag the user never typed.
findings.repro: Ran with mcp-review-check.config.json = {"sarifLocation":"servers/a","quiet":true}: node dist/cli.js --stdio "node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs" --format json. stderr has 'warning: --sarif-location applies only to --format sarif', and nothing for quiet.
findings.fix: Use cliGiven.has('sarif-location') for this warning, as formatWarnings does, or move the check into formatWarnings. Consider the same for the 'tool-args has no effect without --active' warning when both come from the file.

votes.evidence: cli.ts:721 (the finding cites line 688) is `if (values['sarif-location'] !== undefined && format !== 'sarif') stderr += 'warning: --sarif-location applies only to --format sarif'`. It tests the merged values. formatWarnings (cli.ts:205-213) requires `given.has(opt)`, so it warns only for switches given on the command line, and options-and-config.md:34 documents that a config key gets no warning. Reproduced with a config {"sarifLocation":"servers/a","quiet":true} and `--config <file> --stdio good-server --format json`: stderr had 'warning: --sarif-location applies only to --format sarif' and nothing for quiet.

findings.title: `extra-args: --format json` or `--output x` silently replaces the Action's SARIF file, and the upload then fails
findings.claim: The Action puts --format sarif --output <sarif-file> before the extra-args. parseArgs keeps the last value of a string option, so `--format markdown` in extra-args writes markdown into mcp-review-check.sarif, and `--output other` sends the SARIF elsewhere while the step reports sarif-file as the old path, which then does not exist or is stale. upload-sarif then fails or uploads nothing, with an error message that does not point at the cause.
findings.repro: Ran: node dist/cli.js --no-config --format sarif --output x.sarif --format markdown --stdio "node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs". x.sarif begins with '# Acme Notes 1.4.2' (a markdown report).
findings.fix: In the run step, reject (usage(), exit 2) extra-args that contain --format, --output, --json-output or --save-baseline=... for the reserved ones (--format/--output/--json-output), with a message that points at the `sarif-file` input. Alternatively, place the reserved options after the extra-args so they win, and print a ::warning.

votes.evidence: action.yml builds args=(... --format sarif --output "$INPUT_SARIF_FILE" ...) and then appends the extra-args tokens. parseArgs keeps the last value of a string option. `node dist/cli.js --no-config --format sarif --output x.sarif --format markdown --stdio good-server` wrote a markdown report into x.sarif ('# Acme Notes 1.4.2'). So `extra-args: --format json|markdown` passes a non-SARIF file to upload-sarif, which fails with a parse error that does not point at extra-args. One detail is wrong: with `--output other`, the step does not report the old path. It runs `rm -f` on the SARIF file first and sets `sarif-file=` (empty) when the file is missing. The upload step's condition `steps.run.outputs.sarif-file != ''` then skips the upload silently. Nothing reaches code scanning in either case, and nothing warns. ci.md:138 does not say that these options must not go in extra-args.

areas.name: engine architecture (cross-cutting)
areas.coverage: Read at bc7090d in a detached worktree (since removed): src/rules/engine.ts, src/rules/index.ts, src/rules/types.ts, src/rules/util/access.ts, the corpus memo in src/rules/util/text.ts (lines 190-260), the origin cache in src/rules/util/html.ts (lines 60-90), src/report/index.ts, the runRules orchestration in src/cli.ts (lines 760-830), the toolName call sites in src/connect.ts, paginate/listAll in src/protocol/legacy.ts, test/engine.test.ts and test/helpers.ts. Grepped round 1 and round 3 FINDINGS/REMEDIATION for engine items (F123, F124, F125, F133, A04-02, A09-04, A10-05) to avoid repeats. Ran: npm ci and build; a fuzz script with 423 hostile-shape snapshots through runRules(RULES); an end-to-end repro of A13-01 with a raw stdio JSON-RPC server (exit 3 fatal versus exit 1 baseline); the silent-PASS repro for A13-02 through runRules and buildReport; a read-tracking proxy and renderJunit on the auth-required fixture for A13-03; a metadata consistency check (duplicate IDs, finding platforms versus severity keys, empty sources), which found nothing. Not covered: util/net.ts, util/obs.ts, util/schemaWalk.ts, util/ui.ts and util/wwwAuth.ts in detail (other areas own them); the snapshot.ts type definitions beyond coverage; HTTP-path e2e of A13-01 (same toolName call at connect.ts:549, not run); the vitest suites (no single test file was run); the CHANGELOG 1.0.1/1.1.0 text beyond the corpus memo and the deadline changes visible in the code.

improvements.title: Hostile-shape fuzz test for the whole rule catalog
improvements.detail: A vitest that builds snapshots with each server-controlled field (tool/schema/resource/prompt/serverInfo/capabilities/_meta, and names such as constructor/__proto__/toString) set to null, number, array, {}, {"toString":"x"} and parsed __proto__ objects. It runs runRules(snap, RULES) and asserts there are no INTERNAL findings, and also runs the connect-side helpers (toolName). The 423-case script used in this review found A13-01 in seconds. It costs about 1 s of CI time.

improvements.title: Rule-metadata self-test: needs must cover what check() reads
improvements.detail: Run every rule against the auth-required, connect-failed and listing-only fixture snapshots through a read-recording Proxy, the same technique as engine.tracked(). Fail when a rule reads a list, serverInfo, initializeRaw or authProbe that its declared needs do not guarantee and still counts as run. This turns the hand-maintained URL_ONLY set and the A10-05/A13-03 class of bugs into a mechanical check.

improvements.title: Move engine-side rule ID lists into rule metadata
improvements.detail: URL_ONLY (engine.ts:35) hard-codes six rule IDs that the engine treats differently, and the listing-only reason is computed twice (engine.ts:43 in unmetNeed and :211 in runRules). A metadata flag (e.g. `judges: 'url'` or a 'url' Need) plus a single listing check would make a new URL rule correct by construction. Internal refactor, no output change.

improvements.title: Per-rule timing in --verbose and a slowest-rules line
improvements.detail: runRules already reads a clock for the deadline. Recording the elapsed time per rule and printing the top 5 in --verbose (and in JSON under a debug key, or not at all to keep the schema stable) would make the remaining between-rule deadline gap (a single slow rule runs to its end) diagnosable, and help with the A09 quadratic-regex class of reports.

improvements.title: Sort the ignored findings like the reported ones
improvements.detail: runRules sorts `findings` with sortFindings but returns `ignored` in catalog-emission order (engine.ts:259). The JSON report's ignored[] and the JUnit system-out therefore list ignored findings in a different order than the main list. Deterministic, but inconsistent. sortFindings(ignored) is a one-line change.

improvements.title: Declarative custom checks in the config file (local rule pack)
improvements.detail: Teams cannot add organisation policy, e.g. forbidden tool-name patterns, required annotations, or banned _meta keys, without forking. A small declarative schema in the explicit --config only (never a discovered file, see A01-01), with id prefix X-, severity warning/info only per the severity principle, and pattern matching over the existing corpus() data. This gives an extension point without executing user code and without the programmatic API that is listed as Not planned. Additive keys under the 1.x stability policy.

findings.title: A tool whose name is an object with a non-function toString key crashes the whole CLI (fatal, exit 3, no report)
findings.claim: toolName() falls back to String(t.name). For a JSON object such as {"toString":"x"}, String() throws TypeError 'Cannot convert object to primitive value'. connect.ts maps toolName over the re-list and fresh-connection lists outside any try, so the exception reaches runCli as an internal error. The server under test can prevent any report from being written: there is no JSON/SARIF/JUnit output, only 'fatal:' and a stack trace. The same class appears in src/rules/spec.ts:434-435 and 522-523 (String(r.uri), String(p.name)).
findings.repro: RAN. findings.title: A rule that throws is counted as run, becomes an info finding, and leaves the score, coverage and gate as if the check were complete: a crash can turn FAIL into PASS
findings.claim: In the catch block, rulesRun is incremented and an INTERNAL finding with severity 'info' is pushed. It is not added to `scored`, and coverage.toolLevel stays 'ok'. So one input that makes rules throw drops all of their findings for every other tool: the gate passes, the score is computed, and the verdicts are not INCOMPLETE. This conflicts with the project's principle that a check missing data is partial, never a pass, as A10-05 and A04-02 already applied to stops and connect failures. Combined with A13-01, once connect.ts is fixed the same poisoned tool would make 59 rules throw.
findings.repro: RAN (engine plus buildReport via dist, connect bypassed): a snapshot with BAD_TOOLS gives {errors:14, failed:true, score:0, internal:0, rulesRun:94}. The same plus one tool {name:{toString:'x'}} gives {errors:1, failed:false, score:84, internal:59, rulesRun:94, coverage 'ok'}. The other fuzz cases were run too: 423 hostile-shape variants of tool, schema, resource, prompt, serverInfo and capabilities fields; only the toString-object cases threw.
findings.fix: Treat a throwing rule as not run. Push it to skipped with the reason 'internal error: <message>' and not to rulesRun. Mark the result partial: either a new coverage reason or an EngineResult.internalErrors count that buildReport turns into verdict INCOMPLETE and score null, and that --fail-on-incomplete gates. Keep the INTERNAL finding for visibility, but at warning level, or make it fail the run with exit 3 as the help text describes for internal errors.

It computes the score from result.scored, and failed from the gate plus fatal/stopped/incompleteFails, so an INTERNAL finding affects none of them. The CLI exit code (cli.ts:835) is built from these same values. The existing tests (engine.test.ts:29, remediation-wp9-report-redact.test.ts:150) only check that the info finding is emitted, which matches the current behaviour and does not catch the gap. The same rule ID throwing instead gives {rulesRun:1, scored:0, failed:false, score:100, verdicts 'NO AUTOMATED BLOCKERS', cov ok}, so a crash turns FAIL into PASS (exit 0). findings.title: In auth-required / token-rejected runs, rules with needs: [] that judge initialize or list data pass without data (JUnit shows them as passed)

Yet SRV-011, SRV-012, SRV-013, SRV-014, SRV-015, SPEC-002, SPEC-017, SPEC-018, SPEC-020, SPEC-021, SPEC-023 and POL-005 run on undefined or empty data, count in rulesRun, and are written as passed <testcase/> in JUnit. improvements.title: Probe the missing and mismatched MCP-Protocol-Version header and the Mcp-Name check on 2026-07-28 servers
improvements.detail: The streamable-http page has these MUSTs: a header that differs from _meta io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion gets 400/-32020; a modern-only server that does not support pre-2025-06-18 clients rejects a POST without the header; a missing or wrong Mcp-Name on tools/call, resources/read or prompts/get gets 400/-32020. wire.ts probes only a missing or wrong Mcp-Method (headerMismatchNone/Wrong). A version-mismatch probe on tools/list is read-only and safe. A Mcp-Name mismatch can be probed safely on resources/read of a listed URI, or prompts/get, with a mismatched header. Avoid tools/call, because a non-validating server would execute it. Feed the results to SPEC-014 (deterministic MUST, so error).

improvements.title: Check that a notification POST gets 202 with no body
improvements.detail: Both the 2025-11-25 and the 2026-07-28 transports say an accepted notification MUST get 202 Accepted with no body. The SDK sends notifications/initialized, and the tracer sees that exchange, but no rule reads it. A server that answers 200 with a body, or 204, breaks strict clients. Read the existing sdk notification exchange; this adds no new request. Error severity on spec only.

improvements.title: Surface stdio and SDK transport errors that are collected but never used
improvements.detail: RecordingTransport.transportErrors (the first 20 messages) and transportErrorCount are filled on every run but no rule, report field or --verbose line reads them. They hold the SDK's 'unknown message ID' and parse-failure messages: evidence for SPEC-016 (C-02) and for stdout pollution. Report the count in JSON (limits or transport) and in --verbose.

improvements.title: Cite the HTTP+SSE (2024-11-05) transport page in SRV-008 and SPEC-005 findings on sse-legacy servers
improvements.detail: Against a legacy HTTP+SSE server (SDK SSEServerTransport), SRV-008's error links only the 2026-07-28 streamable-http page. The 2024-11-05 transports page has its own Origin MUST, and that page is the one the server owner implements.

findings.line: SPEC-016 id check (e.requestId !== undefined && e.responseId !== e.requestId && e.responseId !== null); fed by collectErrors in src/connect.ts:365
findings.title: SPEC-016 warns when a server rejects a foreign Origin with 403 and a JSON-RPC error body that has no id, which the spec explicitly allows
findings.claim: The 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP page says an invalid Origin MUST get HTTP 403 and the body MAY be a JSON-RPC error response that has no id. The same applies to a rejected notification (400). collectErrors records such a body with responseId undefined. SPEC-016 exempts only id null, so the textbook-correct response produces 'origin evil: response id undefined does not match request id 0' (spec warning). So a server that follows the spec gets penalised on SRV-008's own probe.
findings.repro: A raw 127.0.0.1 server that answers any request whose Origin contains 'evil' with 403 and {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Origin not allowed"}} and otherwise serves 2025-11-25 JSON (initialize, tools/list, 202 for notifications). `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:58503/mcp` gives '! SPEC-016 [spec] server: origin evil: response id undefined does not match request id 0'. The same happens with a 400 status.
findings.fix: For an error response, treat a missing id the same as id null. At least do this when the HTTP status is 4xx, or when the exchange is an Origin, notification or header-validation probe, where the spec permits an id-less error. Keep the mismatch warning only for a present, non-null id that differs from the request id.

votes.evidence: Code path at bc7090d: src/probe/network.ts:200 sends the 'origin evil' probe (initialize, id 0, Origin https://evil.mcp-review-check.invalid) through the tracer. Its label does not start with 'sdk ', so src/connect.ts collectErrors reads it. summarizeJsonRpc (src/protocol/trace.ts:264) sets s.id only when 'id' in o, so an error body with no id gives responseId undefined, and collectErrors pushes {requestId: 0, responseId: undefined}. In src/rules/spec.ts:413 the check `e.requestId !== undefined && e.responseId !== e.requestId && e.responseId !== null` exempts only null, not a missing id, and nothing earlier guards against it (no status check, no origin-probe exclusion). Ran it: I built a worktree at bc7090d and started a 127.0.0.1:58503 server that answers Origin *evil* with 403 and {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Origin not allowed"}} and otherwise serves 2025-11-25 JSON. `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:58503/mcp` printed "! SPEC-016 [spec] server: origin evil: response id undefined does not match request id 0", the exact message from the claim. The Streamable HTTP spec text ("HTTP response body MAY comprise a JSON-RPC error response that has no id") allows this response for an invalid Origin (403) and for a rejected notification (400). So a server that follows the spec gets a spec warning. Neither FINDINGS.md (round 1 and round 3) nor CHANGELOG 1.0.1/1.1.0 covers it: they cover only the result-id case and the code-range policy. Severity: the false positive is only a warning, but it hits exactly the server behaviour that SRV-008 recommends, so medium. Fix: also skip responseId === undefined when the response is an error (or when the HTTP status is 4xx). Worktree removed.

Code at bc7090d. In src/connect.ts the collectErrors function sets responseId to m.id for every error message, so a body with no id gives undefined. In src/rules/spec.ts:413 SPEC-016 checks `e.requestId !== undefined && e.responseId !== e.requestId && e.responseId !== null`. Only null is exempt, not undefined (an id that is absent).

Repro: I built the CLI in a detached worktree. The test server bound to 127.0.0.1:58503 and answered any request whose Origin contained 'evil' with {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Origin not allowed"}}, which has no id. Other requests got normal 2025-11-25 JSON and 202 for notifications. `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:58503/mcp` printed '! SPEC-016 [spec] server: origin evil: response id undefined does not match request id 0' with status 403. It printed the same line with status 400.

Spec check: the 2025-11-25 transports page says "If the Origin header is present and invalid, servers MUST respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden. The HTTP response body MAY comprise a JSON-RPC error response that has no id". It allows the same id-less body for a rejected notification (400). The claim cites the 2026-07-28 page, which I did not fetch; the 2025-11-25 text alone is enough.

So a server that follows the spec gets a spec warning from SRV-008's own Origin probe. It is a false positive that every correct server answering this way will hit, so it is more than cosmetic, but it is only a warning and not an error. Suggested fix: also exempt responseId === undefined (or skip the id check when the response has no id and the HTTP status is 4xx). The worktree has been removed.

findings.title: JSON-RPC responses whose id matches no request (unsolicited responses) are never reported
findings.claim: RecordingTransport.record() ignores a result whose id is not pending. It does store an error with requestId undefined, but SPEC-016 runs its id check only when requestId is defined. MCP and JSON-RPC require every response to carry the id of the request it answers, so a stream of responses to requests that were never sent is a deterministic protocol violation. It passes silently. The SDK's 'unknown message ID' onerror messages go into transportErrors and transportErrorCount, which no rule or report reads (grep finds no consumer outside recording.ts).
findings.repro: A stdio server (scratchpad critic/errflood.mjs) that, after initialize, writes N error responses with ids 100000+i that the client never sent. `node dist/cli.js --stdio "node errflood.mjs 20000" --format json` gives the same findings as N=2000 or a clean server (TOOL-006/011/012/018/028 and SRV-002 only), with no SPEC-016 and no mention of the 20000 stray messages. The run took 0.7 s.
findings.fix: In record(), when m.id is not in pending, record an 'unsolicited response' observation (count plus the first few ids), also for results. SPEC-016 should then warn once ('N responses answered no request'). Either surface transportErrorCount in the report and --verbose, or drop the dead field.

votes.evidence: At bc7090d, recording.ts record() (lines 67-79) adds nothing for a result whose id is not pending. For an error it pushes requestId undefined. SPEC-016 (spec.ts:395-416) then runs only the integer and reserved-range code checks, and checks the id only when e.requestId !== undefined. transportErrors and transportErrorCount are written only in recording.ts; grep finds no reader in rules or report. Runtime check: a raw stdio server (scratchpad errflood.mjs) sent 2000 unsolicited error responses (ids 100000+, code -32603) plus a stray result. It produced exactly the same findings as N=0 (TOOL-006/011/012 error, SRV-002 info x2, TOOL-005 info), with no SPEC-016. JSON-RPC requires the response id to equal the request id, so this violation goes unreported. Low severity, as filed.

findings.title: SRV-008 accepts any non-2xx answer to a foreign Origin, although the spec requires exactly 403
findings.claim: The spec text is: 'If the Origin header is present and invalid, servers MUST respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden.' SRV-008 reports only when originEvil gets a 2xx. A server that rejects the foreign Origin with 400, 404 or 500 gets no finding at all, not even info, although clients and intermediaries cannot tell such a rejection from other failures.
findings.repro: The same raw server as in C-01, but with status 400 for the evil Origin. `node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:58502/mcp --format json` gives no SRV-008 finding. It gives only SPEC-007 (my server ignores the version header) and the C-01 SPEC-016 false positive.
findings.fix: When originEvil gets a 4xx other than 403 and 401 (auth may run before the Origin check), and originNone gets 2xx, report a spec warning: 'foreign Origin rejected with <status>; the spec requires 403'. It is a warning, not an error, because the status could come from another validation.

votes.evidence: server.ts SRV-008 (lines ~233-237) emits a finding for originEvil only when is2xx(evil). A 400, 404 or 500 to the foreign Origin yields no finding, even when originNone is 2xx, so the deviation from 'MUST respond with HTTP 403' is detectable by comparison. The rule's own rationale says 'The spec requires a 403 for an invalid Origin.' originEvil is not read anywhere else (only snapshot.ts type, network.ts probe send). I did not reproduce at runtime because the C-01 server was not available; the gap is clear from the code. It is a conformance-only gap: the foreign Origin is still rejected, so no DNS-rebinding exposure.

findings.title: Non-public IPv6 forms that embed IPv4 and a few reserved ranges count as public
findings.claim: isNonPublicIp returns false for the IPv4-compatible '::127.0.0.1', NAT64 '64:ff9b::a00:1' (10.0.0.1), 6to4 '2002:a00:1::1', the IPv4-translated '::ffff:0:a00:1', discard-only '100::1', deprecated site-local 'fec0::1', Teredo 2001::/32 and 192.88.99.0/24. isLoopbackHost also misses '::127.0.0.1'. These helpers drive SRV-004 (private addresses in public DNS), APPS-005 (CSP naming localhost or a private IP) and the AUTH local-URL checks, so such an AAAA record or CSP origin is not flagged.
findings.repro: node -e "import('./dist/rules/util/net.js').then(m=>['::127.0.0.1','64:ff9b::a00:1','2002:a00:1::1','::ffff:0:a00:1','100::1','fec0::1','192.88.99.1'].forEach(ip=>console.log(ip,m.isNonPublicIp(ip),m.isLoopbackHost(ip))))" prints false false for every address.
findings.fix: Unwrap the embedded IPv4 for ::/96 (compatible), ::ffff:0:0/96, 64:ff9b::/96 and 2002::/16 (bits 16-47), and check it with isNonPublicIPv4. Add 100::/64, fec0::/10, 2001::/32 (Teredo, as non-public) and 192.88.99.0/24.

votes.evidence: net.ts isNonPublicIPv6 recognizes only the IPv4-mapped prefix (::ffff:0:0/96), plus ::, ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, ff00::/8 and 2001:db8::/32. V4_RANGES lacks 192.88.99.0/24. Running the claimed command against the built dist printed 'false false' for ::127.0.0.1, 64:ff9b::a00:1, 2002:a00:1::1, ::ffff:0:a00:1, 100::1, fec0::1 and 192.88.99.1 (the control ::ffff:a00:1 gave true). Consumers: server.ts:139 (SRV-004), apps.ts:179/181 (APPS-005), auth.ts:36 and isLocalTarget. In auth.ts the miss makes the check stricter (the URL counts as non-local), not laxer. Round 1 fixed the IPv4-mapped notation only; these forms are new. Low severity: deprecated or rare forms in heuristic, info/warning-level checks.

findings.title: An option and its value given as one argv word reads 'unknown option --stdio; did you mean --stdio?'
findings.claim: When a script, Dockerfile CMD exec form or package.json passes '--stdio node server.js' as a single argument, parseArgs reports the whole word as unknown. usageMessage cuts the name at the first whitespace (so it does not echo values) and then suggests the same name it just called unknown, which tells the user nothing.
findings.repro: In zsh: S='--stdio node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs'; node dist/cli.js $S (zsh does not split $S) gives 'error: unknown option --stdio; did you mean --stdio?' and exit 2. The same happens with '--quiet --no-quiet' passed as one word.
findings.fix: If the raw unknown token contains whitespace and its first word is a known option, say '--stdio and its value were passed as one argument; pass them as two arguments or write --stdio=<value>'. Never suggest an option equal to the name shown.

votes.evidence: Reproduced at bc7090d. node dist/cli.js '--stdio node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs' prints 'error: unknown option --stdio; did you mean --stdio?' with exit 2. '--quiet --no-quiet' as one word gives 'unknown option --quiet; did you mean --quiet?'. Cause: usageMessage's regex /'(?:-\w, )?(-[^'=\s,]*)/ cuts the option at the first whitespace. closestOption then finds the exact option at distance 0 and suggests it. A true typo (--stdoi) still gets a correct suggestion. This is a UX issue only.

findings.line: line 64 rootCauses(result.scored ?? f) and line 71 score(result.scored ?? f), against counts and verdicts over new findings only; text and markdown with --diff-only
findings.title: With --baseline, the summary mixes a score over all findings with counts and verdicts over new ones; --diff-only removes the only line that explains it
findings.claim: With a baseline that holds every finding, the text report reads 'Score 0/100 · 32 root causes · 0 errors · 0 warnings · 0 info' and 'Claude: NO AUTOMATED BLOCKERS'. The score and root causes include the 50 baselined findings; the counts and verdicts do not. Without --diff-only, one '50 known finding(s) from baseline' line hints at the gap. With --diff-only (the recipe in docs/guide/ci.md) that line is removed, the markdown table shows Score 0/100 next to 0 errors, and the summary nowhere says that findings were baselined. A reader of the job summary sees a contradictory score and a clean verdict for a server with 19 error root causes.
findings.repro: node dist/cli.js --stdio 'node test/fixtures/bad-server.mjs' --save-baseline b.json; then node dist/cli.js --stdio 'node test/fixtures/bad-server.mjs' --baseline b.json --diff-only (text or --format markdown). The JSON summary has score 0, errors 0, rootCauses {errors:19, warnings:13}, baselined 50.
findings.fix: When baselined > 0, label the parts in every format: 'Score 0/100 (all findings, 50 known) · 0 new errors ...' and 'Claude: NO NEW AUTOMATED BLOCKERS'. Keep a one-line '50 known from baseline' count even under --diff-only; the help text says it drops the list, not the count.

votes.evidence: Reproduced. With a baseline saved from bad-server.mjs, `--baseline b.json --diff-only` prints text 'Score 0/100 · 32 root causes · 0 errors · 0 warnings · 0 info' and 'Claude: NO AUTOMATED BLOCKERS · ChatGPT: NO AUTOMATED BLOCKERS · Result: PASS'. The markdown table shows 'Score | 0/100 · 32 root causes' next to 'Findings | 0 errors · 0 warnings · 0 info'. Neither output mentions baselined findings. Source: report/index.ts:64,71 uses result.scored ?? f, and cli.ts:785 sets scored to all findings. Caveat: this split is documented and intended. options-and-config.md line 22 says 'The score still counts every finding', and line 24 says --diff-only drops the 'N known finding(s)' line. So it is not a logic bug. The confirmed defect is presentation: the --diff-only text and markdown summary (the docs/guide/ci.md:62 recipe) shows a contradictory score and counts with no hint that findings were baselined. Low severity, UX.
